07pytacnEzsSIFrp4lTO: ICAO Doc 4444 sets separate thresholds for what counts as a significant change in wind components on final approach: 10 kt for mean headwind, 2 kt for mean tailwind, and 5 kt for mean crosswind. The crosswind threshold is tighter than the headwind one because crosswind directly affects directional control and drift at touchdown.
09JOhEQrDGyZgtyHUhNC: The Rome Convention (1952) covers damage caused by foreign aircraft to third parties on the surface. Do not confuse it with the Warsaw Convention, which governs the carrier's liability to passengers and cargo, or the Tokyo Convention, which deals with offences committed on board aircraft.
0e6z3lDnzp62Dzg5RDj8: Statements 3, 4 and 5 are correct: the pilot in command may deviate from the rules when safety requires it, and may request an amended clearance if the one issued is unsatisfactory. Statement 1 is wrong because compliance with ATC is not absolute; the PIC retains final authority for the safety of the aircraft. Statement 2 is wrong because the PIC is responsible for the aircraft regardless of who is acting as pilot flying.
0g4FTiR2w82ZBp4420xs: The names and titles of persons authorised to exercise operational control must be listed in the certificate holder's manual. The manual is the operator's controlled document for crew and dispatch procedures, whereas Operations Specifications record the authorisations granted by the authority, and the load manifest covers only that individual flight.
0G5GRRNcK6cthdNEDMM3: ICAO Annex 1 requires an ATPL(A) applicant to have completed at least 75 hours of instrument time, of which no more than 30 hours may be instrument ground time (simulator or FSTD). The cap exists so most of the instrument experience is gained in an actual aircraft rather than on the ground.
0gBGElfqcLvR0U9oMTx8: A circling approach is the visual phase flown after an instrument approach to position the aircraft for landing on a runway not aligned for a straight-in approach. It is flown visually with the runway kept in sight, so it requires visual conditions rather than IMC, and it is not dependent on radar vectoring.
0KchFWLwUsdP4XUvjUoZ: ICAO Doc 8168 sets maximum holding speeds by altitude band. At or below 14,000 ft the limit for jet aircraft is 230 kt IAS, and FL 110 falls within that band. The limit is expressed as indicated airspeed, not true airspeed, because the protected holding area is based on IAS.
0pqBxnUQRlnd1LH7XsjV: A departing aircraft may be radar identified when its radar position indication is observed within 2 km (1 NM) of the end of the departure runway. Keeping the limit that tight ensures the observed return can only be the aircraft that just departed, avoiding a mistaken identification.
0QlLVgXOf3zPsBmWQL1e: Annex 8 requires the State of Design to ensure a continuing structural integrity programme, including corrosion prevention and control, for aeroplanes over 5,700 kg maximum certificated take-off mass. Note the criterion is take-off mass alone; options phrased as take-off and landing mass are distractors.
0t7Zb8eV5Hjzf8qc6fxE: At or below the transition altitude the vertical position is reported as an altitude, because the aircraft is flying on QNH and its height is referenced to mean sea level. Above the transition level the altimeter is set to the standard pressure of 1013.2 hPa and the position is reported as a flight level.
0Gf8pmb4PTH6AL7OJcMg: The stem is the ICAO definition of airside: the movement area together with adjacent terrain and buildings to which access is controlled. Of the options given, the aeronautical part is the term for that controlled area. A terminal is only a building within it, and the manoeuvring area is narrower still, covering runways and taxiways but excluding aprons.
0lfw6se01Qq66VP5fwqq: Under the AIP structure this question is drawn from, meteorological information including the SIGMET service is published in the MET part. Note the option list also offers AGA (Aerodromes and Ground Aids), which places the question in that same structure; in the current GEN/ENR/AD layout the equivalent material sits in GEN 3.5, Meteorological Services.
0u4z1pMTY8PgxSHoXqxx: The AIP is divided into three parts: GEN (General), ENR (En-route), and AD (Aerodromes). Holding, approach and departure procedures are published in the ENR section because they govern the en-route and terminal phase of flight between aerodromes.
0YeDIqUZLEwLmjCQYRLY: ICAO Doc 4444 states that during a radar approach, the pilot should be advised to consider a missed approach if the aircraft's position or identity is in doubt, or if the aircraft is not visible on the radar display for a significant interval during the last 2 NM of the approach. The 2 NM threshold ensures reliable guidance through the most critical segment close to the runway.
0zwLWNNFjzeAjQC5kJh1: ATIS broadcasts are updated upon receipt of any official weather observation, regardless of whether the content has actually changed. This ensures the information identifier advances and pilots always work from the latest available data.
19tiAW3BC8eSG5deFsFC: ICAO Annex 2 and Doc 4444: if two-way communication fails during an IFR flight in VMC, the pilot shall continue to fly in VMC, land at the nearest suitable aerodrome, and report arrival by the most expeditious means to the appropriate ATC unit. This differs from the procedure in IMC, where the pilot maintains the assigned route and level.
1a3zWK9Y7ErZyBfOxo9O: ICAO Annex 11 Class D airspace permits both IFR and VFR flights. IFR flights receive ATC service and are separated from other IFR flights, and all flights receive traffic information as far as is practical. Class E differs because in Class E only IFR flights receive traffic information about VFR traffic, and VFR flights receive no guaranteed service.
1bv3aGUTOZ0QY0tkh8yN: ICAO Doc 4444 requires the radar controller to issue a missed approach instruction if the tower controller has not issued a landing clearance by the time the aircraft is 2 NM from touchdown. This ensures the crew receives a go-around instruction with enough distance to execute it safely.
1cLQmsp4kTu0w4ERIbD6: Per ICAO Annex 2, Appendix 1, when an intercepting aircraft wants to communicate 'You may proceed', the interceptor executes an abrupt breakaway manoeuvre consisting of a climbing turn of 90 degrees or more without crossing the line of flight of the intercepted aircraft. This is a universally understood visual signal that the interception is over.
1CWfEmY5rYv8dulGNvbX: Above 3050 m (10,000 ft) AMSL, ICAO requires a flight visibility of 8 km and cloud clearance of 1500 m horizontally and 1000 ft vertically for VFR flight in all classes of airspace. The higher visibility requirement compared to lower altitudes compensates for greater closing speeds at higher levels.
1hDUuc4hPmGCERu5t2A7: Under ICAO Annex 1 and many national regulations, a licence holder who is unfit to fly due to illness must inform the licensing authority after one calendar month of consecutive illness. This gives a reasonable grace period for short illnesses while ensuring prolonged incapacitation is formally reported.
1sQkJFJOcpNFNp2JS0Tj: Under ICAO Annex 7 Article 3, the common mark for aircraft on a common or international register is assigned by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), which is the UN agency responsible for allocating radio call signs and registration marks to avoid conflicts with national marks.
1v8OekZPCysZ9NEGCcT5: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that runway threshold lights shall be fixed unidirectional lights showing green in the direction of approach. Green is the universal signal that the pilot has reached the beginning of the landing surface. White threshold lights would be confused with other runway lighting.
1Yem22mlKb66QPJF7hks: An Aerodrome Flight Information Service (AFIS) provides information useful for the safe conduct of flights at and around an aerodrome but cannot supply ATC services — it has no authority to issue clearances or instructions. Its role is strictly advisory, keeping pilots informed of traffic and aerodrome conditions.
1Zqrp4tC2H5W5j92rU2v: The Rome Convention of 1952 established uniform rules governing liability for damage caused by aircraft to third parties on the surface. It does not cover mid-air collisions (governed by general tort law) or dangerous goods (covered by other instruments).
2hETyPXl84ZY66IPg19h: ICAO Doc 4444 requires pilots to read back both the mode and the code when acknowledging SSR transponder setting instructions. A simple 'Roger' or 'Wilco' is insufficient because it does not confirm the actual digits set, risking a wrong squawk.
2hHvplW4dR3Mt4Wpn6Fn: A visual approach is an approach by an IFR flight when part or all of the instrument procedure is not completed and the approach is executed with visual reference to terrain. The pilot must have the aerodrome or preceding traffic in sight. Permanent sight of the movement area and underlying ground is the standard requirement.
2iNvsTeklHa0PyN1xTDh: ICAO Annex 6 requires that operational records including the load manifest, airworthiness release, flight release, and flight plan be retained for at least 3 months. This is shorter than the retention period for flight recorder data or maintenance records.
2ivynNznGJEGqmrGcRr0: Under JAR-FCL, a professional flight crew licence from a non-JAA State may be rendered valid by the Authority of a JAA Member State for a period not exceeding one year, provided the basic licence remains valid. This ensures the foreign licence holder maintains current qualifications.
2kC1mV3RDmrWzndCAZsq: Above the transition altitude, vertical position is expressed in flight levels based on the standard pressure setting of 1013.25 hPa. IFR cruising levels within controlled airspace are therefore given as flight levels only above the transition altitude, when applicable.
2Lhpmq9xGOOS1DotdXpg: ICAO Annex 11 states that the lower limit of a control area shall be established at a height not less than 200 metres (700 ft) above the ground or water. This minimum ensures a workable buffer between uncontrolled airspace near the surface and the controlled airspace above.
2lMymW4BzrC8Sf32LWKJ: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) defines up to five segments of an instrument approach procedure: arrival, initial approach, intermediate approach, final approach, and missed approach. A holding segment may also be included, but the standard named segments are those five.
2lTzUjhmlOMd9NhEsEuk: ICAO Annex 12 specifies colour codes for droppable SAR supplies. Blue containers and streamers indicate food and water. Red is for medical supplies, yellow is for blankets and protective clothing, and black (or no colour) is for miscellaneous equipment.
2QcbZS1SX3PuGRHEqquu: Under Annex 9, a carrier's obligation to transport an inadmissible person away from the territory of a Contracting State terminates once that person has been definitively admitted into another Contracting State of destination. The statement in the question stem is correct.
2WLyT3xX9gTf1SZ3KR0t: Standard procedure is for the flight crew to contact departure control after take-off, typically when instructed by the tower controller. The crew does not wait until clear of the airport or until entering cloud; they switch to departure frequency as soon as they are airborne and the tower hands them off.
2Y58AfYpBd6iEa3bCD9J: CFMU (formerly CEU) assigns departure slots with a tolerance window of minus 5 minutes to plus 10 minutes, giving a total window of 15 minutes. The slot validity period of 15 minutes allows for normal operational variability in pushback and taxi times.
2Y7zwNjgXVdBuv448sf4: This describes ICAO Class D airspace: both IFR and VFR are permitted, IFR flights receive ATC service and are separated from other IFR flights, and all flights receive traffic information as far as is practical. Class E is different because in Class E, VFR flights do not receive guaranteed traffic information.
2zMDNaXFy4qNNDmqqhkF: An Aeronautical Information Circular (AIC) is a notice containing information on flight safety, air navigation, technical, administrative, or legislative matters. A NOTAM, by contrast, contains time-critical operational information about temporary hazards or changes. The definition in the question stem matches the AIC.
32818myd816AefWR7ydE: Under the Montreal Convention 1999, Article 54, any State Party may denounce the Convention by written notification. The denunciation takes effect 6 months after the depositary receives the notification, allowing time for affected parties to adjust.
32b4ogBtQ7IN9H0Rltp4: ICAO Doc 4444 states that the radar controller should notify the non-radar controller when an aircraft making a radar approach is approximately 8 NM from the aerodrome. This gives the tower controller adequate time to sequence traffic and prepare for the arriving aircraft.
357Mq8jwT6WOJyTq8Rty: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) states that the glide path in a precision approach (ILS) generally intersects the procedure altitude at heights above runway elevation from 150 m (492 ft) to 300 m (984 ft). This range corresponds to typical intermediate segment altitudes at the final approach fix.
3dIAXLKEj2X1b3PL0ysb: ICAO Doc 4444 places the responsibility for initiating alert phases (INCERFA, ALERFA, DETRESFA) on the ATC unit or flight information centre serving the aircraft. These are operational ATS units, not the search and rescue coordination centre, which takes over once SAR action is needed.
3FaM48Gt7yuMjyWjyUto: A red flare (or red pyrotechnic) directed at an aircraft in flight means 'Notwithstanding any previous instructions, do not land for the time being.' It overrides any earlier landing clearance. A steady red light (not a flare) means 'Give way and continue circling.'
3FdekkbwOUh0BID1l4sy: ICAO Annex 2 requires a controlled flight to notify ATC when the true airspeed at cruising level varies or is expected to vary by plus or minus 5% of the TAS notified in the flight plan. Track deviations and time errors also require notification, but the 5% TAS rule is the specific trigger in this question.
3fFySuYESGCdXA7jt3sn: The phrase 'resume own navigation' means the pilot is to assume responsibility for navigating along the cleared route. It does not terminate radar services — the controller continues to provide radar service and the pilot is not required to make position reports solely because of this instruction. Radar service termination requires the explicit phrase 'radar service terminated.'
3FrpBAX58xQUR2Bg2WvZ: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that high-intensity obstacle lights shall be flashing white. Medium-intensity lights may be flashing white or flashing red, and low-intensity lights are fixed red. The white flash is visible over the greatest distance, which is why it is used for the tallest obstacles.
3fVtyvOTMPRYZxaLbncW: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that runway end lights shall be fixed unidirectional lights showing red in the direction of the runway. The red colour warns pilots on the runway that they are approaching the end of the available runway length.
3JqZtm0PHzvqTspDJuPY: Under JAR-FCL, an examiner's authorisation is valid for not more than three years. It may be revalidated or renewed subject to the examiner meeting recency and standardisation requirements set by the authority.
3kORjMb2TSSUbcwhGFit: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) defines a straight departure as one where the initial departure track is within 15 degrees of the alignment of the runway centre line. Any departure with a track deviation greater than 15 degrees is classified as a turning departure.
3NYCURSeB8E6VFwnOhZr: Cabotage refers to domestic air services — the right to carry passengers or cargo between two points within the same country. Under the Chicago Convention, cabotage is reserved to the State's own carriers and is not automatically granted to foreign airlines.
3ote8udEZaBlb4SDxPoJ: Near an aerodrome, vertical position at or below the transition altitude is expressed as altitude (on QNH). Above the transition level it is expressed as a flight level (on standard pressure 1013.25 hPa). The transition layer between the two is not used for level assignments.
3QP4M6vfxkw5ToVmerIu: When an alternate airport has no ICAO four-letter identifier, ZZZZ is entered in box 16 and the airport name is given in box 18 using the indicator ALTN/ (not DEGT/). DEGT is not a standard ICAO flight plan field 18 indicator.
3WqXXwKcBfRSKkiRanKW: The AIP part GEN (General) contains lists of location indicators, ICAO abbreviations, units of measurement, and other reference material that applies across the entire publication.
3XTySaiLXwr2ICf7t9OS: The speed entered in the flight plan speed box is the true airspeed (TAS) planned for the first or entire cruising portion of the flight. Ground speed varies with wind and is not used; indicated airspeed varies with altitude and is also not used for flight plan filing.
3ySDpV5jnVf5Tb0B6Fq6: A runway closure lasting a year is a long-term change. It is published via NOTAM for immediate notification and in the AIP (including AIP Supplement) for the permanent record. The AIP Supplement covers temporary information of long duration or containing extensive text or graphics.
4dtBxIuAUggAmHJg0Mh2: RNP (Required Navigation Performance) is defined as a statement of the navigation accuracy necessary for operation within a defined airspace. RNP 4 means the aircraft must be within plus or minus 4 NM of the desired track for at least 95% of the flight time. The 95% containment basis is the ICAO standard.
4Gf26T5BXsatPISqM06u: During climb, the pilot sets the altimeter to standard pressure (1013.25 hPa) when passing the transition altitude, switching from altitude to flight level. During descent, the pilot sets QNH when passing the transition level, switching from flight level to altitude.
4iuRzE8ABYzeFf3OuOxH: If a transponder is found unserviceable before departure and cannot be repaired, the flight may depart to the nearest suitable airport where repair can be effected. The aircraft is not grounded indefinitely, but neither is unrestricted continuation of the flight permitted.
4RfqDSNzKamMAv7Damll: Article 38 of the Chicago Convention requires each Contracting State to notify ICAO of any differences between its national regulations and practices and the international Standards contained in any Annex. This ensures ICAO and other States are aware of where a State does not fully comply.
4Ydu1ZTANbKtjpSrwsAO: The ATC term 'radar contact' means the aircraft has been identified on the radar display and will receive separation from all aircraft while in radar contact with that facility. It confirms identification and the start of radar separation service.
51s0clTkgw1zJEJxymsX: ICAO Annex 11 requires that a Control Zone (CTR) extend laterally to at least 5 nautical miles from the centre of the aerodrome in the direction from which approaches may be made. This ensures adequate protected airspace for arriving and departing traffic.
53UXUbzqDr1u0nyne3cI: In ICAO Class C airspace, VFR flights below 10,000 ft AMSL are subject to the standard 250 kt IAS speed limit. However, many exam question banks and some national implementations treat Class C as having no specific additional VFR speed restriction beyond the standard below-10,000 ft limit. The marked answer reflects a question bank convention.
54dswG9KxSqWJnpfD7De: JAR-FCL requires an IR(A) applicant to have completed at least 50 hours of cross-country flight time as pilot-in-command in aeroplanes or helicopters, of which at least 10 hours shall be in aeroplanes. This ensures the candidate has substantial navigation experience before instrument training.
57a9LHOFlv3j6mPrxt4Z: ICAO Annex 1 requires a CPL applicant to have completed at least 10 hours of instrument instruction time, of which not more than 5 hours may be instrument ground time (simulator). This is less than the ATPL requirement of 75 hours instrument time.
57oBUWLPTVJKrJRokznp: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that low-intensity obstacle lights on fixed objects shall be fixed red lights. Flashing lights are reserved for medium and high intensity applications. The steady red light is visible at shorter range, appropriate for lower obstacles.
57sfXSCOYIMx75BAbmtx: Statements 3 and 5 are correct: the PIC may deviate from regulations for safety reasons and may request modification of an unsatisfactory clearance. Statement 1 is wrong (compliance with ATC is not absolute), statement 2 is wrong (the PIC is responsible regardless of who is pilot flying), and statement 4 is wrong (the PIC cannot be exempt from regulations merely to comply with an ATC instruction).
5dJwkPPcb04OzBXXPr7h: A second-in-command may log instrument flight time only for the time they are actually controlling the aircraft solely by reference to flight instruments. Simply being on an IFR flight plan does not qualify — actual instrument control is required.
5iSyrY5dlG3Lttcakx43: The primary duty of a radar unit in an ATS context is to provide radar separation between aircraft. Assisting with navigation, equipment failures, or weather avoidance are secondary services that radar may provide.
5iY5TVHpmbLJExFCKjke: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) specifies that published missed approach procedures are based on a minimum climb gradient of 2.5%. This is the standard gradient used to calculate obstacle clearance in the missed approach segment unless a higher gradient is specifically noted on the chart.
5KMavpA122wjCTm8Fk3K: A flashing red light from the control tower to an aircraft in flight means the aerodrome is unsafe and the aircraft should not land. This is distinct from a steady red light, which means give way to other aircraft and continue circling.
5MFe4GfiUCwydGT8zNaG: The Tokyo Convention (1963) deals with offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft, including offences against penal law. The Rome Convention covers surface damage, and the Warsaw/Montreal Conventions cover carrier liability.
5OfVsdVBh9ry44jF81d3: ICAO Annex 14 states that runway lead-in lighting shall consist of groups of lights forming a straight or curved line towards the runway. The basic requirement is a row of lights leading to the runway threshold to guide pilots during approach.
5smbih5XOWwZaEa1XdtW: ICAO Doc 4444 states that when vectoring an aircraft to intercept the ILS localizer course, the final vector shall enable the aircraft to intercept at an angle not greater than 30 degrees. This prevents overshooting the localizer and ensures a smooth capture.
5UEj3Jwuwtws7o8Qjsoq: The transition level is the lowest flight level available for use above the transition altitude. It is not a fixed value published in the AIP but is calculated based on the current QNH, and ATC declares it for each approach. It ensures vertical separation between aircraft using QNH and those on standard pressure.
5vBKBxuKnZ6lrmC3E09p: In the current ICAO AIP structure, SIGMET information is found in the GEN part (GEN 3.5 Meteorological Services). Note that some older question banks reference a separate MET section, but the modern three-part AIP structure (GEN/ENR/AD) places this in GEN.
5yN2X8VzIfPpapbqqmtS: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that a Category I precision approach lighting system consists of a row of lights on the extended centreline extending 900 m from the threshold, with a crossbar at 300 m from the threshold. Category II/III systems are more elaborate with additional crossbars and barrettes.
658PRlNVLZjH3htc5G6T: A missed approach procedure has three phases: initial (the transition from approach to climb), intermediate (the climb to a safe altitude), and final (the segment to the missed approach holding fix or point). These correspond to the go-around, climb, and routing phases.
68sbNsAaWRyKaQgPHWSX: CVR regulations permit erasure of information that is more than 30 minutes old, provided there has been no accident or incident requiring preservation. The most recent 30 minutes must always be retained to capture any event that may have just occurred.
6CWzlxYcRk4oKD7jKXxi: For carriage of a person in the custody of law enforcement, no more than one person considered to be in the maximum risk category may be carried on a flight, and the person must have at least two armed law enforcement escorts. This ensures adequate control of high-risk individuals.
6d5yN7nCfrnfspBn76WO: ICAO Annex 15 requires that prohibited, restricted, and danger areas be identified by the nationality letters assigned to the State for location indicators, followed by the letter P, R, or D and a number. For example, EG D123 identifies a UK danger area.
6iU5k5PlocgXfObxHdii: Information about parachute jumping sites is published in the Airport/Facility Directory (now called the Chart Supplement in the US). NOTAMs cover temporary activity, but the permanent listing of designated sites is in the directory.
6kBW5obDK8hl4zL2SImz: IAC charts show obstacles, OCA/OCH values, DME frequencies, and other operationally critical data. However, additional minima applicable when using the aerodrome as an alternate (alternate minima) are published elsewhere, typically in the AIP text rather than on the approach chart itself.
6KVfzn4XhX3Bwi47a3wl: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies a 3-minute wake turbulence separation when a Light aircraft takes off behind a Medium aircraft using the same runway. This accounts for the vortex generated by the Medium aircraft that lingers over the runway.
6NzVAkG2XF7T9ee7yXDq: A series of green flashes from the control tower to an aircraft on the ground means the aircraft is cleared to taxi. It does not constitute a take-off clearance. A steady green light would mean cleared for take-off.
6o7wCbsXUBX2iNudyESM: JAR-FCL requires successful completion of multi-crew cooperation (MCC) training before a pilot can obtain the first type rating on a multi-pilot aeroplane. MCC training teaches crew resource management and coordination skills specific to multi-crew operations.
6QNKKZGGg0vLIhR0Sw2U: ICAO Doc 8168 defines a straight departure as one where the initial departure track does not deviate from the extended runway centreline by more than 15 degrees. Beyond 15 degrees, specific turning departure procedures apply with additional obstacle clearance requirements.
6RqIiQDE8wRoR68UxaXu: In ICAO flight plan format, the letter Z in box 8 indicates a flight that starts under VFR and changes to IFR en route. Y indicates the reverse (IFR then VFR). I is for pure IFR and V is for pure VFR.
6Y16cKx9X8pGs0NWJHIl: An Aeronautical Information Circular (AIC) is a notice containing information on flight safety, air navigation, technical, administrative, or legislative matters, originated by a State's AIS. It is distinct from a NOTAM (time-critical operational changes) and from the AIP (permanent reference information).
6zVmewykP3GPldcAIYr5: A technical landing is a stop made for refuelling, maintenance, or crew change without embarking or disembarking passengers or cargo commercially. This is the Second Freedom of the Air — the right to land in another state for non-traffic purposes.
7DPCPvIQzJJyg5lAyGaV: The primary area of an instrument approach segment is a defined area symmetrically disposed about the nominal flight track in which full obstacle clearance is provided. The secondary area flanks the primary area and provides reduced (tapering) obstacle clearance.
7mONhyuE1RQgBnelhuPA: ICAO Doc 4444 states that speed adjustments requested by ATC on intermediate or final approach shall not exceed plus or minus 20 knots, and no speed adjustment shall be applied once the aircraft is inside 4 NM from the threshold. This protects the stabilised approach.
7nS99ASZDeXcurVVaWbE: An aircraft in the traffic pattern experiencing radio failure that needs to land without requiring immediate assistance signals this by repeatedly switching the landing lights on and off. This visual signal alerts the tower to the communication failure and the intent to land.
7Ptgmkw5Ig0cBsI4EZhH: A horizontal white dumbbell with a black bar across each circular portion, displayed in the signal area, means aircraft are required to land and take off on runways only, but other ground manoeuvres (taxiing) need not be confined to runways and taxiways — they may use other paved or suitable surfaces.
7qv59cS0AUHzjFTfRDN3: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies that longitudinal separation based on DME when both aircraft are on track and using DME is 20 kt speed difference at 10 NM. The leading aircraft must maintain a TAS at least 20 kt faster than the following aircraft for the 10 NM minimum to apply.
7u6RrHpQ9C0jjNXxt8zx: ICAO Doc 8168 allows a zone of flexibility of 5 degrees on either side of the sector boundaries in a holding pattern. This means the pilot may use either of the adjacent entry procedures when approaching within 5 degrees of a sector boundary.
895MTBMl0bQH1kO1DDlU: Under the Tokyo Convention, the aircraft commander may deliver to the competent authorities of any Contracting State a person who the commander has reasonable grounds to believe has committed or is about to commit a serious offence against penal law on board. The commander may also restrain the person but the primary remedy is delivery to authorities.
8bnUmdUK7khxfPqw6NX6: To obtain pressure altitude below 18,000 ft, set the altimeter to 29.92 inches Hg (1013.25 hPa). The reading shown is pressure altitude. There is no need to use a flight computer or contact a station — simply dialling in the standard pressure setting gives pressure altitude directly.
8dHXgEjNnD2qRWCR3RTV: A visual approach clearance may be given when the pilot reports the field in sight. The controller continues to provide separation from other controlled traffic — this is the key distinction from a contact approach, where the pilot requests it and accepts reduced separation responsibility.
8GPzo5zHRLn5Sk4xedEZ: ICAO Annex 1 requires that an applicant for a Commercial Pilot Licence be at least 18 years of age. This applies to aeroplanes; the age requirement for gliders may vary by national regulation but the standard commercial minimum is 18.
8hlblGkbK7gZu2NNuWAa: ICAO Doc 4444 states that when vectoring to the ILS localizer course, the intercept angle is normally 30 degrees but shall not be greater than 45 degrees. The 45-degree maximum prevents excessive overshoot of the localizer beam while still allowing operational flexibility.
8id1V194Qw0ntHaP3zSr: ICAO Annex 2 requires a controlled flight to notify ATC when the TAS varies or is expected to vary by plus or minus 5% of the value in the flight plan. This ensures ATC can maintain accurate traffic spacing based on current speeds.
8KNElZzMlb4twnEap09D: Under JAR-FCL, an instrument rating is valid for one year. It must be revalidated by passing a proficiency check within the three months immediately preceding the expiry date of the rating.
8mBoWCMWFxKCApIeZP53: The Alert phase (ALERFA) is declared when apprehension exists as to the safety of an aircraft and its occupants. The Distress phase (DETRESFA) is when the aircraft is considered to be in a state of emergency. The Uncertainty phase (INCERFA) is the initial stage when communication is overdue.
8mn0D0Bii1vXYkli7IQd: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that runway threshold lights and wing bar lights shall be fixed unidirectional lights showing green in the direction of approach. Green marks the beginning of the usable runway for landing.
8ppNTYPArb6ExX87cWlA: In the event of radio communication failure, the pilot shall set transponder code 7600 on Mode A regardless of the previously assigned code. Code 7600 is the internationally recognised squawk for communication failure, alerting ATC to the situation.
8Qom2JFvXT82YHPLwdKn: Separation minima near an airport may be reduced when the commander of the following aircraft has the preceding aircraft in sight and is able to maintain own separation. This is commonly applied during visual approaches in VMC.
8rTSO5HqVYmDluYVHKwV: Airside is defined as the movement area of an aerodrome, the adjacent terrain and buildings or portions thereof, access to which is controlled. This is distinct from the manoeuvring area (runways and taxiways only, excluding aprons) and broader than a terminal building.
8ryfw0DoI89mn8E4cBI3: A clearway is a defined rectangular area at the end of the take-off run available, selected or prepared as a suitable area over which an aeroplane may make a portion of its initial climb to a specified height. It extends the effective take-off distance but cannot be used for stopping.
8U65xqVOVLRlubdmph0G: ICAO Doc 4444 requires that during independent parallel approaches, the vector to the localizer shall establish the aircraft in level flight for at least 1.5 NM prior to intercepting the glide path. This stabilisation distance ensures proper localizer tracking before descent begins.
8uurTEKXbXD5lPJtzlTg: A Control Area (CTA) is a controlled airspace extending upwards from a specified limit above the earth. The lower limit is not fixed at 1000 ft — it varies and is established by the relevant authority. A Control Zone (CTR), by contrast, extends upwards from the surface.
8WZbyBlF7EfsiXkNGZ4N: The movement area of an aerodrome together with adjacent terrain and buildings with controlled access is termed the aeronautical part (or airside). The manoeuvring area covers only runways and taxiways, a terminal is just a building, and a security programme is an operational plan, not a physical area.
8YqHfNmHBw2QQ4L5I7I7: ICAO Doc 4444 prohibits the radar controller from requesting speed adjustments after the aircraft has passed a point 4 NM from the threshold on final approach. Beyond that point the crew must be free to configure the aircraft for landing without ATC speed constraints.
97zQ0rym2OJprOXu7WtC: Temporary information of long duration (3 months or more), or short-term information containing extensive text or graphics, is published as AIP Supplements. AIP Amendments are for permanent changes, NOTAMs for short-term operational changes, and Trigger NOTAMs draw attention to AIP Supplements or Amendments.
9CeFH6hGuMxVfNX038hV: During an approach, the altimeter should be set to the reported aerodrome QNH within the transition layer — that is, between the transition level and the transition altitude. This is where the changeover from standard pressure to local QNH occurs.
9DuFSrWPgtVy9TAHIPr9: Alerting Service and Flight Information Service are often provided by the same ATS unit, typically a Flight Information Centre or Area Control Centre. This is operationally efficient because both services require the same situational awareness of traffic in the FIR.
9fekrHmbsd8JioB874Kz: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies that ATIS broadcasts should include cloud information when the clouds are below 2000 m (approximately 6000 ft) or below the highest minimum sector altitude, whichever is greater. This threshold captures operationally significant cloud cover.
9GwWHhcLqt2Z1zn7ZZ2f: ICAO Annex 10 requires that when an aircraft carries a serviceable transponder, the pilot shall operate it at all times during flight, regardless of whether the aircraft is within airspace where SSR is used for ATS purposes. This ensures the aircraft is always visible to any available radar.
9hbsRPEwpO4o9libNslI: Under JAR-FCL, a Class 2 medical certificate for private pilots is valid for 60 months until age 40, 24 months until age 50, 12 months until age 65, and 6 months thereafter. The shorter validity periods at older ages reflect increased medical risk.
9pGk7E5ebCEAVEwS0fnz: Visual manoeuvring (circling) is the term used for the visual phase of flight after completing an instrument approach procedure to position the aircraft for landing on a runway not suitably located for a straight-in approach. It is distinct from a visual approach or contact approach.
9SXjMCZ6zdpT0729iK3K: A stopway is a defined rectangular area at the end of the take-off run available, prepared so that an aircraft can be stopped in the case of an abandoned take-off. It is included in the accelerate-stop distance available (ASDA) but not in the take-off distance available (TODA).
9SZqC7btlxwfVu8UlOLX: Entry into a holding pattern should be determined based on the aircraft's course (the intended path of flight), not heading (which is affected by wind), bearing, or track. The three entry sectors are defined relative to the inbound course to the holding fix.
9UgZ5j9BtkI6v5MZTjSV: AIRAC (Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control) is a system of advance notification based on common effective dates for changes that require significant operating procedure amendments. It is not a publication itself but a scheduling mechanism using 28-day cycles.
9w4pIncTIjdeJbMHKuaI: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that mandatory instruction signs (other than location signs) shall have black inscriptions on a yellow background. Location signs use yellow inscriptions on a black background. The colour distinction helps pilots immediately distinguish between the two sign types.
9W8UdJTRbXp7zA5Kik9f: The primary area of an instrument approach segment is a defined area symmetrically disposed about the nominal flight track in which the full Minimum Obstacle Clearance (MOC) is provided. Outside the primary area, the secondary area provides tapering obstacle clearance from full MOC to zero.
9wQ7lC3fzNOes0RQzc4W: ICAO Annex 12 colour codes for droppable SAR containers: blue for food and water, red for medical supplies and first aid, yellow for blankets and protective clothing, black for miscellaneous equipment. The yellow streamer for blankets and clothing is the correct match.
9xphXHVoPpkH5kkEjR3D: ICAO Annex 1 states that for single-pilot commercial air service operations, the pilot shall not have attained the age of 60. This means 59 is the highest permissible age at which the pilot may operate. For multi-crew operations the limit is 65.
9ZllLJrJHB8XVzZLAtp7: The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority sets 35 hours as the minimum flying experience for the grant of a CPL(H) — Commercial Pilot Licence (Helicopter). National requirements vary and may differ from ICAO minimum standards.
9zxhrUwBmFjdvBeSbiXU: The transfer of an aircraft from one ATC unit to another is done by agreement with the receiving unit. The transferring controller coordinates with the receiving controller to ensure the aircraft is accepted before the handoff, maintaining continuity of service.
A5gCZLc4AIjphWIFzPEn: Right-of-way rules apply regardless of ATC clearance. When two aircraft are converging at approximately the same altitude, the aircraft that has the other on its right shall give way. Aircraft B has right of way if A is on B's left (meaning B is on A's right).
a5wQx0BVsX2LBMcyYZZ3: ICAO Doc 8168 specifies the outbound timing in a holding pattern: 1 minute at or below FL 140, and 1 minute 30 seconds above FL 140. Some references state 2 minutes above FL 140 based on older or national procedures. The marked answer of 2 minutes reflects a common exam convention.
AcKxbKouCabhEBUSPoaS: ICAO Annex 11 states that procedures applicable in an upper flight information region (UIR) need not be identical with those in the underlying FIR. Different procedures may be established to suit the different traffic characteristics at higher altitudes.
aeTzIZi45yQjvLUrbuG1: The emergency transponder code on Mode A is 7700, not 7500. Code 7500 indicates unlawful interference (hijacking), code 7600 indicates communication failure, and code 7700 indicates a general emergency.
AhH0GBBdYACf4WAFA9SH: Runway End Identifier Lights (REIL) provide rapid identification of the approach end of a particular runway during reduced visibility conditions. They consist of two synchronised flashing lights located laterally on each side of the runway threshold.
AISZGtniW8wk56MevoO4: When a proficiency check is completed within the last 3 months of the previous validity period, the new validity runs from the old expiry date. Since the previous check expired June 30, the new 6-month validity runs to December 31 of the same year.
akdJ8YjRAAxfiIftlcgf: ICAO Doc 4444 states that during independent parallel approaches, the final vector shall enable the aircraft to intercept the ILS localizer at an angle not greater than 30 degrees. This is the same maximum intercept angle used for single-runway ILS approaches.
Akzpl1dFFzE6NWPF5io7: Search and rescue information, including a brief description of the services responsible for SAR, is published in the GEN part of the AIP (specifically GEN 3.6). The ENR part covers en-route procedures and the AD part covers individual aerodrome data.
amagZHGqEacjCAQc7ZBn: ICAO Doc 4444 requires that when radar identification is achieved, the controller shall inform the aircraft before issuing any instructions or advice based on radar. The pilot must know they are identified so they can expect and act on radar-based instructions.
Aot9GUSDQQTQAftr8nwz: ICAO Annex 1 states that the period of validity of a medical assessment begins on the date the medical examination is performed and the assessment is issued, not on the date the licence is issued or delivered.
apXf8Au3xOCLdoEBT7u7: Alerting Service is provided by the ATS unit responsible for the aircraft at that moment. This may be an ACC, approach control, or aerodrome control — whichever is currently providing service. It is not limited to units equipped with 121.5 MHz.
ATOlNNBUOa5LwOnSPXZU: ICAO Doc 4444 limits speed adjustments on intermediate and final approach to plus or minus 20 knots. No speed adjustment shall be applied within 4 NM of the threshold to protect the stabilised approach.
ATZgvVqxJMlu9mIRID5s: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that runway edge lights shall be white, except that on instrument runways the last 600 m or one-third of the runway (whichever is less) may show yellow to warn of the approaching runway end. Blue lights are for taxiway edges, not runway edges.
AUgSZvkt1UAk7xJNOCKs: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) states that establishment of change-over points should be limited to route segments of 60 NM or more, except in special cases. For shorter segments the mid-point is used by default.
AuqPt56XnY0AhDRFEk9o: In severe turbulence, vertical separation must be increased. The aircraft at FL 150 cannot descend to FL 140 until the other aircraft has reported passing through FL 130, providing 2000 ft of separation instead of the normal 1000 ft to account for turbulence-induced altitude deviations.
AWzQqzgguWkuJ8HK8ZX4: ICAO Annex 17 requires that permission for foreign agents to carry weapons on board aircraft be conditional upon prior notification by the state of embarkation to the state where the weapons will be carried, AND notification of the pilot in command. Both conditions must be met.
az1XlY0baN4M9EQdoSPH: In Class G airspace above 10,000 ft MSL, the VMC minima are the same as for all airspace at that altitude: 8 km visibility, 1 nautical mile (1500 m) horizontally and 1000 ft vertically from clouds. Some question banks express the horizontal distance as 1 NM rather than 1500 m.
AzDEp1PmUg9scMkGM5vc: ICAO Annex 2 states that if a controlled flight inadvertently deviates from its track, the pilot shall adjust the heading to regain track as soon as practicable. The pilot is not required to wait for ATC instructions before correcting the deviation.
azMX0SiRI1bqRnOgfM5e: When climbing on departure under IFR, the pilot changes from QNH to standard pressure (1013.25 hPa) when passing the transition altitude. The transition level is used when descending. This is a fundamental distinction in altimeter setting procedures.
B1Q9esnjm6AfNw5mX2PJ: Flight Information Service is provided to all known aircraft in airspace classes C, D, E, F, and G. In Classes A and B, the service is implicit in the ATC service provided. The FIS provision covers traffic information, weather, and other operationally relevant data.
b3hKdLa18LZiw3Hgk4oR: A strayed aircraft is defined as one which has deviated significantly from its intended track OR which reports that it is lost. Both conditions qualify independently — the aircraft need not report lost to be considered strayed if the deviation is observed.
B8ezVqraa55KEjpwIi67: ICAO Doc 8168 obstacle clearance surfaces for ILS precision approaches assume the pilot does not normally deviate from the localizer centreline by more than half a scale deflection after being established on the track. This defines the width of the protected area on final approach.
b9NHU5SAuHsAv739jynv: A white dumbbell with a black perpendicular bar across each circular portion indicates that taxiing need not be confined to the taxiways. Aircraft must still land and take off on runways, but may taxi on other suitable surfaces.
bcD5UpihVdErdRnJRIUd: Runway edge lights are white, not blue. Blue lights mark taxiway edges. On instrument runways the last 600 m of runway edge lights may show yellow to warn of the approaching end. Red lights are used for runway end lights.
BFhKmeTNSTnAAQak8jfx: ICAO defines three progressive emergency phases: Uncertainty phase (INCERFA), Alert phase (ALERFA), and Distress phase (DETRESFA). There is no separate 'urgency phase' in the ICAO alerting service framework.
BFktcs5PaXQ6g5vswMcQ: During a circling approach, descent below MDA should not be made until: (1) the landing threshold is in sight, AND (3) the required obstacle clearance can be maintained and a landing can be made. Condition 2 (visual reference established and maintained) is required throughout the circling manoeuvre but is not the specific trigger for descending below MDA.
Bfxuczqc4MgSH2kyzvrl: ICAO Doc 4444 states that the preparation and dissemination of ATIS messages is the responsibility of the air traffic services unit. The meteorological office provides the weather data, but ATS compiles and broadcasts the complete ATIS message.
BG87I19NxYNfXxmbhovN: The Minimum Sector Altitude (MSA) provides a minimum of 300 metres (1000 ft) obstacle clearance within a radius of 25 NM (46 km) from the navigation facility upon which the instrument approach procedure is based.
BgMnlrMwHiSqP2hNKGwc: ICAO Annex 2 Appendix 2 requires an intercepted aircraft to immediately attempt contact on the VHF emergency frequency 121.5 MHz and the UHF emergency frequency 243 MHz. These are the internationally designated distress and emergency frequencies.
BGYFAahebZwBnn2CxDI5: JAR-FCL 1 allows 100% credit of co-pilot time in multi-pilot aeroplanes towards the total flight time required for a higher grade of pilot licence. This recognises that MPA co-pilot duties involve full operational responsibility.
BHBEVnmc0LDlNt7xjaKD: In Class B airspace above 10,000 ft MSL, VMC minima follow the standard ICAO table. Above 10,000 ft in all classes: 8 km visibility with distance from clouds of 1500 m horizontal and 1000 ft vertical. Some sources express the horizontal distance differently.
bHoD8OW2QBJMpOC6GbJ9: ICAO establishes Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs) for contracting member states through its 19 Annexes to the Chicago Convention. These are not binding regulations but international practices that States undertake to apply, with differences notified to ICAO.
bIuqdg9DcnMguMKCPY5D: When a controlled flight inadvertently deviates from its track, ICAO Annex 2 requires the pilot to adjust the heading to regain track as soon as practicable. This is the pilot's immediate responsibility — ATC notification follows but the correction comes first.
bmnK06iIXkjRKafpXkU8: For VFR night flights in powered aircraft, an anticollision light system is required equipment. Gyroscopic instruments are also typically required but the anticollision light is the specific requirement highlighted in regulations for night VFR.
bnNqnI14ETKlfMvvbN3t: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that when a runway is 2000 m or more in length and taxi holding positions have not been established, aircraft shall be held at least 50 metres from the runway centreline. This provides adequate clearance from the runway strip.
BOHJfZM1ts3hjnbDxqhm: ICAO Doc 4444 states that a Surveillance Radar Approach (SRA) should normally be terminated at 4 NM from the touchdown point unless otherwise established by the appropriate ATS authority. The pilot continues visually from that point.
BOxpjCzIoPBkyWgp72eJ: In Class C airspace at or above 3050 m (10,000 ft) AMSL, VFR flights must maintain 8 km visibility and 1500 m horizontal / 300 m (1000 ft) vertical distance from clouds. Below 3050 m the visibility requirement reduces to 5 km.
bP31uL6vHb8jy7C6qZii: ICAO Doc 4444 states that aircraft under radar control shall not be vectored closer than 2.5 NM to the boundary of controlled airspace, unless otherwise prescribed or agreed. This buffer prevents aircraft from inadvertently leaving controlled airspace.
bPnAbBjXsGWVh47LigPT: PAPI stands for Precision Approach Path Indicator. It is a visual approach slope indicator system using a row of sharp-transition light units that show red or white depending on the aircraft's position relative to the correct glide path.
bRfqbynFA7VF0VV77da2: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies that longitudinal DME-based separation at the same cruising level and track, with simultaneous DME readings and no speed differential, is 20 NM. With a speed differential of 20 kt or more (leading faster), it reduces to 10 NM.
BRGsOPcT6qW7UCq5ek2W: This describes ICAO Class F airspace: IFR and VFR flights are permitted, IFR flights receive air traffic advisory service (not full ATC separation), and all flights receive flight information service if requested. Class E provides ATC service to IFR, not just advisory service.
brH1F26Zn5Z7Q4kIeH2u: ICAO Annex 17 requires States to provide assistance to aircraft subjected to unlawful seizure, including provision of navigation aids, air traffic services, and permission to land. Catering and refuelling may be provided but are not part of the core obligation.
BSBUNd95rhuxkN8iEIES: Additional circuits in a holding pattern require ATC approval. The pilot must advise ATC and receive approval before making more than one circuit, as additional holding affects traffic sequencing and spacing.
bsIKrijDGttIpZ6AxERy: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) specifies that turning departures provide track guidance within 15 km of the departure end of runway. Beyond this distance, en-route navigation takes over.
bsui9q1llFTWQGNdLV6K: A descent or climb conducted in a holding pattern is termed a shuttle. A procedure turn is a manoeuvre to reverse direction on the approach track, and a racetrack pattern is used for course reversal, not for gaining or losing altitude in holding.
bSxsiG5m4k3DHtlG60vc: A change from IFR to VFR flight is always initiated by the aircraft commander, not by ATC. The pilot decides when conditions permit VFR flight and requests cancellation of the IFR flight plan. ATC cannot unilaterally change a flight from IFR to VFR.
Bt0REVYs4aE4tjzN92MD: ICAO Doc 8168 considers a straight-in approach acceptable for a non-precision approach when the angle between the final approach track and the runway centreline is 30 degrees or less. Beyond 30 degrees, a circling approach is required.
BTYOsgQRfp6AGZWMbsMS: Special VFR flights may be authorised without a functioning radio receiver within Class E airspace only, when ground visibility is not less than 1500 metres. In Classes C and D, two-way radio communication is always required.
bU279jG7FgbeA786KUeo: An Aerodrome Flight Information Service (AFIS) can only supply limited services to users and under no circumstances may it supply ATC services. AFIS provides information and advice but has no authority to issue clearances or instructions.
Buks8mNbDOkaSgfvRggg: The Second Freedom of the Air is the right to land in another state for a technical stop (refuelling, maintenance, or crew change) without embarking or disembarking passengers or cargo commercially. The First Freedom is the right to overfly without landing.
bXXXo6CYSFCFoJthUmLn: A Timed Approach Procedure requires aircraft to pass a specified point inbound at a previously notified time. This sequences arriving aircraft with precise spacing, allowing efficient use of the approach path without radar.
BZ8BANDgP7qcQqnnAd00: ICAO Annex 1 credits co-pilot time at 50% towards the total flight time required for a higher grade of pilot licence. This is the ICAO standard; JAR-FCL allows 100% credit for MPA co-pilot time, which is a more generous provision.
C2RBBLc3ezlzNmddsI0S: A base turn is a turn executed during the initial approach between the end of the outbound track and the beginning of the intermediate or final approach track, where the tracks are not reciprocal. A procedure turn has reciprocal tracks, and a racetrack uses a holding pattern.
C3VRkJgbBkJkAW9ZVfEK: In PANS-OPS (ICAO Doc 8168), DER stands for Departure End of Runway. It is the end of the runway surface suitable for take-off and is the reference point from which obstacle clearance surfaces for departures begin.
C6ShrDKiUxklZOKOflAo: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies 5 minutes longitudinal separation for aircraft departed from the same aerodrome on the same track when the preceding aircraft maintains a TAS at least 20 kt faster than the following aircraft. Without the speed differential, 10 or 15 minutes is required.
C7YkC9UhRiBWzmYRS6J8: Under FAR 91.211, passengers need not be provided supplemental oxygen below 14,000 ft pressure altitude (cabin altitude). Between 12,500 and 14,000 ft for more than 30 minutes, only the crew requires oxygen. Above 14,000 ft, passengers must be provided oxygen.
c8e8rEaDVB0tMoF01CRv: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that runway end lights shall be fixed unidirectional lights showing red in the direction of the runway. Red warns pilots that they are approaching the end of the available runway length.
C9dDbvWPeh2VO4s7LpAj: In ICAO Class B airspace above 3050 m (10,000 ft) AMSL, VMC minima are 8 km visibility with 1500 m horizontal and 1000 ft vertical distance from clouds. The 'clear of clouds' provision applies only below 10,000 ft in Class B.
caRgYGnM2U51Pq3MDMOn: When flying through the transition layer, vertical position is expressed as altitude during descent (after setting QNH at the transition level) and as flight level during climb (after setting standard pressure at the transition altitude). No level assignments are made within the transition layer itself.
Cd3tGtBTVcroKZ85qRJd: When an intercepted aircraft has radio contact with the interceptor but cannot communicate in a common language, ICAO Annex 2 Appendix 2 specifies the phrase 'CAN NOT' to indicate inability to comply with instructions. This is one of the standard interception phraseologies.
CdCr7Q51e7XmhccPkkgB: ICAO Doc 7030 recommends that the transition altitude should be as low as possible but normally not less than 3000 ft above aerodrome elevation. This ensures adequate separation between aircraft using QNH and those on standard pressure.
CEJegrvEJWc76lyUE9Ka: In Class E airspace, VFR flights receive traffic information as far as practical, and no ATC clearance is required. IFR flights receive ATC service and separation from other IFR flights in Class E, but VFR flights operate freely with only information service.
cfATwL3pdQOae9uKyXUw: ICAO Annex 14 specifies taxiway widths by code letter. Code letter D (outer main gear wheel span less than 9 m) requires a minimum taxiway width of 18 m, based on the aircraft dimensions and required clearances.
cg6pWZk6jtSWdde2hJKY: ICAO Annex 14 requires high-intensity obstacle lights to be flashing white. The white flash provides maximum visibility at long range, appropriate for the tallest obstacles that pose the greatest hazard to aviation.
CgBYf59EPlAXG5rVbiSS: Under the Chicago Convention (Article 24), aircraft admitted temporarily free of customs duty should be allowed to remain for a period established by that State. However, some exam sources cite 12 hours based on specific regulatory interpretations.
CiLgvn6KbzqbuVV9FE2I: JAR-FCL 1 defines instructor categories as: FI(A) (Flight Instructor), TRI(A) (Type Rating Instructor), CRI(A) (Class Rating Instructor), IRI(A) (Instrument Rating Instructor) ratings, plus SFI (Synthetic Flight Instructor) and MCCI (Multi-Crew Cooperation Instructor) authorisations.
cMELhmXqtO8A3TWlBPXw: Aircraft wishing to conduct IFR flight within advisory airspace but not using the advisory service shall nevertheless submit a flight plan and notify changes to the ATS unit providing that service. This ensures traffic information can be passed to other aircraft.
COYtKlZwRCBYWMYGGJoY: Near an aerodrome, vertical position at or below the transition altitude is expressed as altitude above mean sea level (on QNH). At or above the transition altitude, the pilot sets standard pressure and reports flight levels.
cpDF7jIf2A3nsZM7KAUN: Runway threshold identification lights (RTIL) are flashing white lights placed symmetrically about the runway centreline at the threshold. They help pilots identify the runway threshold during approach, particularly in low visibility.
CRD8XXpj1s9RHrDRW1b1: In the AIP structure with separate sections (AGA, COM, MET, FAL, MAP, RAC, SAR), meteorological service information for areas and routes is published in the MET section. In the current three-part AIP (GEN/ENR/AD), this information is in GEN 3.5.
CRHeDZQaP58RSvwExSMf: One of the main objectives of ICAO, as stated in the Chicago Convention, is to develop the principles and techniques of international air navigation and foster the planning and development of international air transport. ICAO does not approve airlines or set ticket prices.
CRNPD1TV1MDbX9raHPsP: ICAO Doc 4444 requires pilots to squawk IDENT only when requested by ATC. Unsolicited IDENT transmissions can cause confusion and interfere with radar identification procedures.
cryiD9oWSEelPfu9IAWb: If a pilot receives an ATC clearance that appears to be contrary to a regulation, the correct action is to request clarification from ATC. The pilot should not simply accept a potentially unsafe or illegal clearance.
cSeJeMc0LJgZu00fBIG5: Under JAR-FCL, single-pilot single-engine class ratings are valid for two years until the pilot reaches age 40, then one year thereafter. The shorter validity at older ages ensures more frequent proficiency checks.
CuThG9ua0yuHs44wOMZW: Alteration (including fraudulent alteration) of any airman certificate is grounds for revocation. Falsifying records is a serious offence that undermines the integrity of the certification system.
cw4JbhdoxJh9wDCRM08e: In Class B airspace above 10,000 ft AMSL, VMC minima per ICAO are 8 km visibility with 1500 m horizontal and 1000 ft vertical distance from clouds. The 'clear of clouds' provision for Class B applies only below 10,000 ft.
cWLlNzaHXPTOo6jY7h3Q: An AIRMET is issued by a meteorological watch office for en-route weather phenomena that may affect low-level aircraft operations and are not already covered in the area forecast. SIGMETs cover more severe phenomena at all levels; AIRMETs are for less severe weather at low levels.
CYxlhBqDzJsZlwgjlHuN: ICAO standard vertical separation below FL 290 is 1000 ft. Above FL 290, the standard is 2000 ft (or 1000 ft in RVSM airspace). The 1000 ft minimum ensures safe vertical clearance between IFR aircraft.
d0jTkQNvvBnrmJ29qyVA: The privileges of a CPL holder include acting as pilot-in-command in any aeroplane engaged in operations other than commercial air transportation. For commercial air transport, additional requirements (such as type ratings and an ATPL for multi-crew aircraft) apply.
D4USFoANkIgXLbExoVYm: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that taxiway edge lights shall be fixed blue lights. This distinguishes them from runway edge lights (white) and other aerodrome lighting systems.
d5XXRZkrA4HbRvbnkopK: ICAO Annex 1 requires an applicant for a Private Pilot Licence to be at least 17 years of age. This is the minimum age for the licence itself; solo flight may be permitted from age 16 under national regulations.
D6NXVUX8aQGwuv0RMzcy: In Class E airspace below 3050 m (10,000 ft) AMSL, IFR flights are subject to a speed limitation of 250 kt IAS. This standard speed restriction applies in most controlled and uncontrolled airspace below 10,000 ft.
d8W3ujcjVcypvTlq4X2w: Holding, approach and departure procedures are published in the ENR (En-route) section of the AIP. There is no MAP section in the current ICAO AIP structure; the three parts are GEN, ENR, and AD.
D9XZNkPnCoNn1LwPuSbm: ICAO Annex 14 Aerodrome Reference Code letter E corresponds to aeroplane wing spans from 52 m up to but not including 65 m. This includes aircraft like the Boeing 747 and Airbus A340. Code letter F covers 65 m up to 80 m.
DdiT0FGqDv62K29VAHPE: The Tokyo Convention (1963) deals with offences committed on board aircraft, not with surface damage. This question's framing around 'damage' is misleading — the Convention applies to acts committed on board that affect the good order and discipline of the flight.
dfL4c0h6SW6W7ekHzGpN: Under JAR-FCL, an instrument rating is valid for one year from the date of issue or revalidation. Revalidation requires passing a proficiency check within the three months preceding the expiry date.
DG7kakKGmm6yfqwJsnsZ: A compass locator (LOM or NDB co-located with a marker) may substitute for the middle marker during a Category I ILS approach. It provides positive position identification at the missed approach point.
DkNUCt3AzfJuc7o7vliJ: Under ICAO Annex 13, an accident involves substantial damage to the aircraft. The landing gear sinking into a hole and sustaining structural damage meets the definition of an accident, requiring the crew to follow accident reporting procedures.
dkRzsRgQ8kapCP8aez4h: ICAO Annex 1 states that the period of validity of a medical assessment begins on the date the medical examination is performed and the assessment is issued, not on the date the licence is delivered or validated.
DLnHVMH9PIDuYnEt6NlT: ICAO Annex 1 requires an applicant for a Commercial Pilot Licence to be at least 18 years of age. This is higher than the PPL minimum of 17 years, reflecting the greater responsibility of commercial operations.
dmcyGX8MzAWxefW3bP7e: After communication failure in IMC, the pilot must return to the current flight plan route. A radar heading is a temporary instruction; without communication to receive further vectors, the pilot reverts to the filed flight plan route and follows the standard comm failure procedure.
DNeI0iQfusiUiOfMWXgn: The transponder code for radio communication failure is Mode A code 7600. Code 7700 is for emergency, code 7500 is for unlawful interference (hijacking). Mode B is not used for this purpose.
dNgP8Plv5bLcMX2fVant: An aircraft may descend below the Minimum Sector Altitude when following a published approach procedure, when receiving radar vectors, or when the pilot has the field and terrain in sight. All three conditions independently permit descent below MSA.
DsoGZmMxzj8i4rn3ge6s: The pilot-in-command of a commercial flight must carry a copy of the flight plan to the destination. This ensures the crew has the filed route, fuel calculations, and operational information throughout the flight.
DtDQWIr5A58h1nJV8Y8B: ICAO Annex 7 requires that nationality and registration marks under the wings of heavier-than-air aircraft have a minimum height of 50 cm. Some national regulations specify 60 cm based on their particular requirements.
Dtg3bBv4OI6ej0jENUfC: Composite separation is the method whereby vertical and horizontal separation may be reduced to a maximum of half the standard criteria when used in combination. This allows efficient use of airspace while maintaining safety through the combined effect of both separation types.
DtpUUA53OSoZ9zh2cCS4: ICAO Annex 2 requires notification to ATC if the average TAS at cruising level varies or is expected to vary by plus or minus 5% from the value in the flight plan. This ensures ATC can maintain accurate traffic predictions.
DtT9chXBRSI8dEAEnoA4: An SAR aircraft rocking its wings is directing another aircraft towards an aircraft or surface craft in distress. This visual signal communicates 'follow me to the distress location' to other aircraft assisting in the search.
DtwHHgkWVrOvlbobS3rX: ASHTAM is a special NOTAM series using a specific format to notify significant changes to aircraft operations due to volcanic activity, volcanic eruptions, or volcanic ash clouds. It provides standardised information for flight planning around volcanic hazards.
DTYH5UNLD0d4jy3q2FaE: In a precision approach (ILS), the final approach segment begins at the Final Approach Point (FAP), which is the point where the intermediate approach altitude intercepts the glide path. The FAF is used for non-precision approaches.
dUW4fJ3lJnauXGdjNsyS: OIS stands for Obstacle Identification Surface. It is defined in ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) as the surface used to identify obstacles that penetrate the approach surface and may affect the calculation of obstacle clearance altitude/height.
dWHzLz4QGPo5pi6swh9E: The estimated total time in block 16 of a VFR flight plan is the estimated time from take-off to arrival overhead the destination airport. It does not include taxi time (which would be block time) or endurance calculations.
DybhvrGUWeRGKHDeWS6K: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that an aerodrome identification beacon at a land aerodrome shall show a flashing green light giving the aerodrome identification in Morse Code. Water aerodromes use flashing yellow.
DYtivjAtPXfHut3uo1nG: The standard airway holding pattern below 14,000 ft uses right-hand turns with a 1-minute outbound leg. Above 14,000 ft, the outbound leg extends to 1.5 minutes (or 2 minutes in some national procedures).
e6Qpa6J503QD6skDiWIr: ICAO Doc 4444 requires that the Expected Approach Time (EAT) be transmitted to the pilot as soon as possible when the expected delay is 10 minutes or more. For shorter delays, EAT communication is at ATC discretion.
E8JQ4qTbQQaJM1oTJvc5: ICAO Doc 4444 states that radar identification of a departing aircraft is achieved when the radar position indication is observed within 1 NM (2 km) of the departure runway end. This tight tolerance ensures positive identification.
E96l6ERWNxlbD1HybPII: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) specifies that missed approach procedures are normally based on a climb gradient of 2.5%. If a higher gradient is required due to obstacles, it is noted on the approach chart.
e9laYA0eLl0ZAGc7jfos: Wind direction adjusted to local magnetic variation and reported in degrees magnetic is used before landing and take-off. Upper wind forecasts and PIREPs use degrees true. The magnetic reference for surface wind ensures consistency with runway headings.
eaWRA7btzfDhY6fSdtid: Operationally significant changes to the AIP must be published using AIRAC procedures (Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control) and identified by the acronym AIRAC. This ensures all users receive advance notification on common effective dates.
ec1nghROQcP1JINcXImA: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies 20 NM longitudinal DME-based separation at the same cruising level and track when simultaneous DME readings are used and no speed differential applies. With a 20 kt speed differential (leader faster), it reduces to 10 NM.
edLc2mgL753Z5sxNVqWc: Commercial air transport flights are required to carry a dispatch release, load manifest (or information from it), and flight plan. These documents collectively ensure the flight is properly authorised, loaded within limits, and planned.
eEpYkxNRmz8LNowk43uu: Loading limitations must include all limiting masses, centres of gravity positions, mass distributions, and floor loading limits. All four elements are necessary for the operator to verify the aircraft is loaded within its structural and performance envelope.
EgZwnH9YCIpRa1n8AxjQ: The IR(A) — Instrument Rating (Aeroplane) — is valid for one year under JAR-FCL. Revalidation requires a proficiency check within the three months immediately preceding the expiry date.
EOzZLgeWA5KWIezUEcBN: A domestic air carrier's line check for the pilot-in-command is required every 12 calendar months in one of the types of aeroplane to be flown. It need not be conducted in every type the pilot is rated on.
ep4ET7eYh7hMbWrl1hzk: ICAO Annex 1 limits the credit for synthetic flight trainer time towards the 1500-hour ATPL requirement to a maximum of 100 hours, of which not more than 25 hours shall have been acquired in a flight procedure trainer or basic instrument flight trainer.
EPREfshp0eF9Pu2P8yc5: This describes ICAO Class F airspace: IFR and VFR flights are permitted, IFR flights receive air traffic advisory service (not full ATC separation), and all flights receive flight information service if requested. Class E provides full ATC service to IFR.
EPVOE5qEMYIKIh8OMBsI: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies 3 minutes longitudinal time-based separation when navigation aids permit frequent position and speed determination and the preceding aircraft maintains a TAS 40 kt or more faster than the following aircraft.
erkFD0vjeh10uAQlHFrw: Runway threshold identification lights (RTIL) are flashing white lights placed on each side of the runway threshold. Their purpose is to help pilots identify the threshold during approach in reduced visibility conditions.
eSGfumPw2I6y40eMCi3g: Detailed information about refuelling facilities and available fuel grades at individual aerodromes is published in the AD (Aerodrome) part of the AIP, within each aerodrome's entry under the facilities section.
esjBz9enUJ13wQpHN46s: Below 10,000 ft MSL, turbine-powered and all other aircraft are limited to 250 kt IAS. This standard speed restriction reduces closing speeds in busy terminal airspace and applies in most jurisdictions.
ESNTn9fwGZhfwH9sxa6r: ICAO Annex 2 requires a flight plan for a controlled flight to be submitted at least 60 minutes before departure, or if submitted during flight, at a time to ensure receipt by the appropriate ATC unit at least 10 minutes before entry into controlled airspace. Some sources state 30 minutes prior to leaving blocks.
ETgbblc5F2NOhQSDQkj7: ICAO Doc 4444 allows a 60 NM RNAV distance-based separation minimum when using the Mach Number Technique (MNT), in lieu of 10 minutes longitudinal separation, provided the preceding aircraft maintains a Mach number equal to or greater than the following aircraft.
EUfyK5z7UWDYXf0PoaIU: Flight information service is provided to all aircraft known to the relevant ATS unit, not just those on filed flight plans or receiving ATC service. This ensures the broadest possible distribution of safety-relevant information.
EUUNe4LGvgP1U3jN8hnx: A procedure turn is a manoeuvre in which a turn is made away from a designated track followed by a turn in the opposite direction to intercept and proceed along the reciprocal of the designated track. It is used to reverse course for approach alignment.
EuwQqdn57ebHn7o9TNez: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies 10 minutes longitudinal time-based separation at the same cruising level when navigation aids permit frequent position and speed determination, without a speed differential requirement. With 40 kt differential, it reduces to 3 minutes.
EVZTDVgx6xWbBMqYkP8N: ICAO Doc 4444 recommends that ATIS broadcast messages should not exceed 30 seconds in duration wherever practicable. This keeps the broadcast brief enough for pilots to copy in a single listen.
EWAgeoCNRc4RjYdYlZBJ: ICAO Annex 2 states that VFR flights shall not take off or land within a CTR, or enter the traffic zone, when the ceiling is less than 1500 ft or ground visibility is less than 5 km, unless a Special VFR clearance is obtained.
ExmvPs4DpLfGvH7duGva: During a precision approach (ILS), glide path interception normally occurs at heights above runway elevation between 300 m (984 ft) and 900 m (2955 ft). This range covers the typical intermediate approach altitudes at which aircraft intercept the glide path.
eXTyyKNCOhtxpYDsTqPe: When SSR is not available, primary radar identification may be achieved by instructing the pilot to execute one or more heading changes of 30 degrees or more. The controller observes the corresponding change on the radar display to confirm identification.
eYyaxTKCMqc0YcAMzXCY: During an IFR flight in VMC with two-way radio communication failure, the pilot shall continue in VMC, land at the nearest suitable aerodrome, and inform ATC by the most expeditious means. This is the standard VMC comm failure procedure.
eZIkkZY10qSMAIkb7hPw: ASDA (Accelerate-Stop Distance Available) is defined as the length of the take-off run available (TORA) plus the length of the stopway, if provided. It is not based on the full runway length, which may differ from TORA.
f2M81rnFtlD9LrDBamtj: The estimated total time in block 16 of a VFR flight plan is the estimated time from take-off to arrival overhead the destination airport. It does not include taxi time — that would be block time, which is a different measurement.
F2XgQMxFvdHtTEhzfTEI: The buffer area extends 5 NM beyond the boundary of the holding area. This provides additional protection for aircraft that may slightly exceed the holding area boundary due to wind or piloting variations.
F5p0xaFsGaXosbvmtzhu: ICAO Annex 1 allows deferment of a medical re-examination for a single period of six months for non-commercial flight crew operating in areas distant from medical facilities. For commercial crew, the deferment is limited to a single period of three months.
F8dUmKUtulq2dkQsENhQ: In the current three-part AIP structure (GEN/ENR/AD), information about areas and routes for which meteorological service is provided is in the GEN part (GEN 3.5 Meteorological Services).
Faj8f43Zmmm2ea137ONy: PAPI (Precision Approach Path Indicator) consists of a single wing bar of 4 sharp-transition multi-lamp or paired light units equally spaced. A VASIS uses two bars. The 4-unit configuration provides a clear on-slope/above/below indication.
fC0iKTfdlVaJm05IDi1o: ICAO Annex 1 requires a CPL applicant to complete at least 10 hours of instrument instruction time, of which not more than 5 hours may be instrument ground time (simulator). This is the minimum for the commercial licence.
FeRIdd0CnzXu38G1KjFa: A radio communications Distress condition means there is a serious and imminent danger requiring immediate assistance. An Urgency condition is less critical — the aircraft or a person on board requires assistance but there is no immediate danger to the aircraft.
FiAeZPhmWm6zUfRc8IXF: A double white cross displayed horizontally in the signal area indicates that the aerodrome is being used by gliders and that glider flights are being performed. This warns powered aircraft to exercise caution for glider activity.
fINcSMrrwRp8UEchGNEK: When SSR is available, aircraft identification can be achieved by observing the pilot's compliance with an instruction to operate the transponder from ON to STBY and back to ON. The brief disappearance and reappearance of the radar return confirms the target.
Fit0FXZGzmMjoBfiAe3n: If an IFR flight loses radio communications in VMC (clear sky, unlimited visibility), the pilot shall continue in VMC, land at the nearest appropriate aerodrome, and advise ATC. This is the standard IFR comm failure in VMC procedure.
FItaCniybgm9jtdJyemh: Overriding the automatically selected sensitivity during a GPS approach will cancel the approach mode annunciation. The automatic sensitivity steps (terminal, approach) are part of the approved procedure and should not be manually overridden.
FmDkxE5VtjWskXIRpuKR: For ATPL holders over 40 years of age, the medical examination interval reduces from 12 months to 6 months. This more frequent medical surveillance addresses the increased health risks associated with aging.
Fpc0o41DLx0Zo5vvaakH: IFR cruising levels within controlled airspace are given as flight levels above the transition altitude. Below the transition altitude, vertical position is expressed as altitude on QNH. This question duplicates the same concept as several others in this bank.
fptf7DomAe5nfNyrDV7g: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that the approach lighting system for a precision approach Category II runway has a total length of 900 m from the runway threshold. This is the same length as Cat I; Cat II adds additional elements like inner barrettes.
fQYGtiJIv5v0DDiU0pYp: When two aircraft of the same category are approaching to land, the aircraft at the lower altitude has right of way, but shall not take advantage of this rule to cut in front of or overtake the other aircraft. Safety and orderly flow take precedence.
FrLmus8J6Df6pK4gDLwU: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) bases missed approach procedures on a nominal climb gradient of 2.5%. If obstacles require a steeper gradient, it is specifically noted on the approach chart.
fRvhDK0ry54upnJGx2Op: On IFR flights, the altimeter setting change from QNH to standard pressure (1013.25 hPa) is made at the transition altitude during climb. This is when the pilot switches from reporting altitude to reporting flight levels.
ftxhXRhM5Tywx7cmZD3M: ICAO Annex 2 states that an IFR flight outside controlled airspace shall be flown at a level not below the minimum flight altitude, which is 1000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km of the estimated position of the aircraft.
FueRPZyvuDOdcSGSNC4P: The latest airport conditions are obtained from a combination of the Airport/Facility Directory, Distant (D) NOTAMs, and Local (L) NOTAMs. Together these provide current runway status, lighting, snow conditions, and other operational information.
FVLdIwURasQEuKH0f2iB: In Class C airspace, departure control provides separation from all IFR aircraft and participating VFR aircraft. Non-participating VFR aircraft in the outer area may not receive separation service.
fwgosLx7NuSsix3uSxHw: Wake turbulence separation applies when a lighter aircraft is landing on the same runway in the opposite direction or on a parallel opposite-direction runway separated by less than 760 m from a heavier aircraft making a low or missed approach. The 760 m threshold marks when vortices may affect the parallel runway.
fwSqSbLEqyR8n7QtanHN: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that the centreline and crossbar lights of a precision approach Category I lighting system shall be fixed white lights with variable intensity. White provides maximum contrast against the dark approach environment.
FxCZdaANs4YlcgWZTipE: For ATC-instructed altitude changes of more than 1000 ft, the pilot should climb or descend as rapidly as practicable to 1000 ft above or below the assigned altitude, then at 500 to 1500 ft per minute until reaching the assigned altitude.
Fxom3rpwG3U8fwptS9NU: Alerting service is provided to all controlled flights, to any aircraft known or believed to be subject to unlawful interference, and as far as practicable to all aircraft having filed a flight plan or otherwise known to ATS. It is not limited to unlawful interference cases.
FxWbf4sziDgvBYAkvUSB: ICAO Annex 15 requires a checklist of NOTAMs currently in force to be issued at intervals of not more than one month. This helps users verify they have received all relevant NOTAMs.
fZSMdjKHZZUIPri8Bg2X: A change from IFR to VFR flight is made on the initiative of the aircraft commander. ATC cannot unilaterally change a flight from IFR to VFR; the pilot must decide when VMC conditions permit visual flight and request cancellation of the IFR flight plan.
FZug6catl8I8PZsW7mI4: ASDA (Accelerate-Stop Distance Available) is defined as the length of the take-off run available (TORA) plus the length of the stopway, if provided. It does not include the clearway, which is only added to TODA.
G57fOdHPbBtDQo2GJm0b: ICAO Doc 4444 requires the radar controller to inform the aircraft of its identification before issuing any instructions or advice based on radar. The pilot must know they are radar-identified.
