g6R9nwq7PhN5Z356SC6N: The marshalling signal for 'apply parking brakes' is: arms down, palms facing inwards, moving arms from extended position inwards. This is part of the standard ICAO marshalling signals in Annex 2.
GbxidmXrmg0nOMcUWdJr: ICAO Annex 7 prohibits registration mark combinations that might be confused with urgent or distress signals. TTT is the urgency signal in Morse code and must not be used as a registration mark combination.
GcK1TmTjzcKwTIsNtuFB: The ATC term 'radar contact' means the aircraft has been identified on the radar display and radar flight instructions will be provided until radar identification is terminated. It confirms both identification and the start of radar-based service.
gCUQEkE88VjdDPCaZ5E9: ICAO Annex 11 lists ATS units as: Area Control Centre (ACC), Advisory Centre, Flight Information Centre (FIC), Approach Control Office, and Aerodrome Control Tower (TWR). An ATS Reporting Office may also be established.
gd9H0n7bvb8nrPE0Vv0T: ICAO Annex 1 requires ATPL applicants to have at least 200 hours of cross-country flight time, of which 100 hours shall be as PIC or co-pilot performing PIC duties under supervision. These thresholds ensure adequate navigation and command experience.
Ge5DFsFX3nHMFdOhCG0C: ICAO Annex 2: in mountainous areas where no State minimum IFR altitude is established, an IFR flight shall maintain at least 2000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km of the estimated position. For non-mountainous terrain the minimum is 1000 ft within 8 km.
GEffJgoxEM8YEalIBTqg: The description matches an AIRMET, not a SIGMET. An AIRMET covers specified en-route weather affecting low-level operations that is not already in the area forecast. A SIGMET covers more severe phenomena at all flight levels.
GERm66BCHVll5gqEg0E1: A series of red flashes from aerodrome control to an aircraft on the ground means 'taxi clear of the landing area in use.' This differs from a steady red light (stop) or a red flare (do not land, directed at aircraft in flight).
GezCEspJNJqZRc2sw1Be: ICAO standard holding patterns use right-hand turns unless otherwise published. All turns in the holding pattern, after initial entry, should be to the right unless the chart or ATC specifies left-hand turns.
gg7IUDRJc4w9OxnPkDV9: During a visual approach in Class C controlled airspace, ATC continues to apply separation with all traffic — both IFR and VFR. Class C provides separation service to all participating flights.
gITh3EFxF0GBKYHjuX9v: ICAO defines three progressive emergency phases: Uncertainty phase (INCERFA), Alert phase (ALERFA), and Distress phase (DETRESFA). There is no separate urgency phase in the alerting service framework.
gJAy2SaVku10UJjC6zwk: ICAO Annex 2 requires notification to ATC when the TAS varies by plus or minus 5% of the value in the flight plan. Track deviations and time estimate errors also require notification but are separate triggers.
GKlxopaJewUYTtrI7KTy: ICAO Annex 2 states that if a controlled flight is delayed 30 minutes beyond the estimated off-blocks time, the flight plan should be amended or cancelled and a new one submitted. The 30-minute threshold uses off-blocks time, not departure time.
GKUt9b7sKNvInBfp4KuM: In a precision approach Category I lighting system, the single, two, and three light source sections on the centreline have specific lengths. The 200 m dimension refers to the segment arrangement of the centreline barrettes.
gNFcEeurGBTdSvyvz1DW: ICAO Annex 14 states that aerodrome lights may be turned off provided they can be brought back into operation at least one hour before the expected arrival of an aircraft. This lead time allows for system checks and warm-up.
goHjown0mLAJAnAzvnRW: Taxiway centreline lights (other than exit taxiway lights) are fixed green lights. This distinguishes them from taxiway edge lights (blue) and runway centreline lights (white).
GOUjwQEzCz5pDZuZVvem: In Class E airspace, VFR flights do not require an ATC clearance or two-way radio communication. VFR aircraft operate freely with traffic information provided as far as practical. Only IFR flights require ATC service in Class E.
gpaQ5fYTcScSMyqjxGb2: The Minimum Sector Altitude (MSA) provides at least 300 m (984 ft) obstacle clearance within a radius of 25 NM from the navigation facility on which the instrument approach procedure is based.
GrklhhKX20bj0vYZqb4k: ICAO Annex 6 requires that weight records (after weighing and CG determination) be preserved for a period of 3 months. This is the minimum retention period for such operational records.
Grtm8iqHm7HrcggBWEo5: ICAO Doc 4444 requires a minimum radar separation of 1.0 NM when independent parallel approaches are being conducted, until aircraft are established on the ILS localizer or MLS final approach track.
gs5ufdlHBskZYuKKfh8j: Taxiway edge lights are fixed blue lights per ICAO Annex 14. Blue distinguishes taxiway edges from runway edges (white) and taxiway centreline (green).
gSfciLslK0dRV6W8Omuz: ICAO Doc 4444 states that during a radar approach, the aircraft should be directed to execute a missed approach if no landing clearance has been received by the time the aircraft reaches a distance from touchdown. Some references cite 2 NM, others 4 NM depending on the type of radar approach (PAR vs SRA).
gspnO1Xrs4DlLHbf7Y43: At night, a pilot who observes a ground distress signal should acknowledge by switching landing lights on and off twice, or if not equipped with landing lights, by switching navigation lights on and off twice.
gTyBmK1XtVXnPBMXpPjP: ICAO Annex 13 states that the sole objective of accident or incident investigation is the prevention of future accidents and incidents. It is not intended to apportion blame, establish liability, or provide evidence for court proceedings.
guOFDPAzBsbU3Ajcakgs: IFR cruising levels within controlled airspace are given as flight levels above the transition altitude when applicable. Below the transition altitude, altitude on QNH is used.
guYTpb1SpVvPsgpKFzyB: A braking action coefficient of 0.25 and below is classified as Poor. Medium is approximately 0.26 to 0.29, Medium/Good is 0.30 to 0.35, and Good is 0.40 and above.
GVzy34aXoQuzkg7H2suc: For a non-precision or circling approach, the Minimum Descent Height (MDH) cannot be lower than the Obstacle Clearance Height (OCH). The OCH sets the absolute floor based on obstacle clearance requirements.
GW8t2nfYKCqLjioH9F9O: ICAO Doc 4444 states that during a radar approach, the pilot should be advised to consider a missed approach if the aircraft is not visible on radar for a significant interval during the last 2 NM. This ensures guidance through the critical final segment.
gYnGVm73rZ0mkL9JSpED: ICAO Doc 4444 states that RNP shall be prescribed by States on the basis of regional air navigation agreements. This ensures consistency across adjacent FIRs and international routes.
h4vddrOGCU7Ti3Cgoeft: If a pilot cannot conform to the prescribed holding procedure, they should advise ATC as early as possible. ATC can then provide alternative instructions or adjust spacing for other traffic.
H51uW1U4lZUaeUrapIf5: The Aerodrome Reference Code consists of a number (1-4, based on reference field length) and a letter (A-F, based on wingspan and outer main gear wheel span). Valid combinations include 2B but not 5E or 6D, as numbers only go to 4.
h8SNpRe8H658hVLqLHdU: In an offset entry into an omnidirectional racetrack procedure, the time on the 30-degree offset track is limited to 1 minute. This prevents the aircraft from drifting too far from the holding fix.
hAGlr56RxpZV5Ry09cDl: OCA (Obstacle Clearance Altitude) is referenced to mean sea level. OCH (Obstacle Clearance Height) is referenced to the aerodrome elevation or threshold elevation. The distinction between altitude and height references is fundamental.
HBeW0ZUX4W1AGZZ9aiwj: In Class C airspace below 10,000 ft AMSL, IFR flights are subject to the standard 250 kt IAS speed limitation. This applies to both IFR and VFR traffic in most jurisdictions.
hBR2eV2RRsu5VFr7wvr4: In the Aerodrome Reference Code, code element 2 (the letter) identifies both the aircraft wingspan and the outer main gear wheel span. Both dimensions determine the required taxiway widths and runway strip dimensions.
hC2GuAnzrZhBoYpLTlfQ: A Flight Information Region (FIR) is an airspace within which Flight Information Service and Alerting Service are provided. These two services are always provided together within a FIR.
hCuDMoCrxRMtwcxVZSja: The ASHTAM volcano colour code RED indicates a volcanic eruption in progress with ash plume/cloud reported or expected above FL 250. ORANGE indicates heightened unrest with potential for eruption. YELLOW is elevated unrest above known background level.
hEFSCQnUwMKscUxDfMFv: A flashing red light from the control tower to an aircraft approaching to land means the aerodrome is unsafe and the aircraft should not land. A steady red light means give way and continue circling.
HFRRpbtvV61nI8v7MOs9: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) specifies the minimum obstacle clearance (MOC) for the initial approach segment primary area as 300 m (984 ft). The intermediate segment MOC is 150 m and the final approach segment varies by approach type.
hilIb7e3lj0xsJ37If0z: ICAO Annex 15 states that a checklist of NOTAMs currently in force should be issued at intervals of not more than one month. The 28-day AIRAC cycle is a separate scheduling mechanism.
HJh8jYSBQn4ibe3AgQ0T: Some national authorities credit 100% of MPA co-pilot time towards total flight time for a higher grade licence. This contrasts with the ICAO Annex 1 standard of 50% credit. The answer depends on the regulatory framework being tested.
hNBnWlklXpjxyxjVu0J5: During an arrival procedure under IFR in VMC, the pilot-in-command is responsible for traffic avoidance. In VMC, the see-and-avoid principle applies even for IFR flights receiving ATC service.
Hp9QZXMGywbcLL9Uip7t: Runway threshold identification lights (RTIL) are flashing white lights at each side of the threshold. They provide rapid visual identification of the approach end of the runway.
HpA3jVtLtmyiEKnqLRpP: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies 20 NM as the longitudinal DME-based separation minimum for two aircraft at the same level using the same on-track DME station, with no speed differential.
hPqhi0nascIolnxY3UIO: Effective scanning for traffic involves systematically focusing on different segments of the sky for short intervals (2-3 seconds each). Continuous sweeping is less effective because the eye needs brief fixation to detect targets.
Hr3oSY8xDUsxxsqGlME4: ICAO Doc 4444 allows 2-minute separation between departing aircraft on the same track when the preceding aircraft is 40 kt or more faster than the following aircraft. For a 20 kt differential, 5 minutes is required.
hrWJ61ylUYtEmS0l4snc: ICAO Doc 4444 requires the Expected Approach Time (EAT) to be transmitted when the expected holding time is 10 minutes or more. For shorter delays, EAT communication is at ATC discretion.
Ht94gkhjJ3qw6QtrCqbp: During independent parallel approaches, a minimum vertical separation of 300 m (1000 ft) should be maintained until aircraft are established on the ILS localizer or MLS final approach track.
hUtTzgCnXW0FFwmABJKE: ICAO Annex 7 specifies that marks on the fuselage and vertical tail surfaces of heavier-than-air aircraft shall have a minimum height of 30 cm. Under-wing marks require a larger minimum of 50 cm.
huxYKo8R7yQehSoagSh5: ICAO Doc 4444 states that a pilot may expect to receive landing clearance or an alternative instruction before the aircraft reaches 2 NM from the touchdown point during a radar approach.
hVyCso2cZOcqFUt5keV7: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that the fixed distance marking, when provided, shall commence at 300 m from the threshold. This marking helps pilots judge their landing point relative to the threshold.
hWIoKHXIAiX5nq0xvrmz: ICAO Doc 4444 states that speed adjustments on intermediate and final approach should not exceed plus or minus 20 kt, and no speed adjustment should be requested within 4 NM of the threshold.
HWozcyoejXvpkVVCfFLS: PAPI consists of a single wing bar of 4 sharp-transition multi-lamp or paired units equally spaced. Two wing bars would be a T-VASIS or AT-VASIS system.
HzWWBtpTeaOfPQYHiT8p: ICAO Annex 12 colour codes for droppable SAR containers: yellow for blankets and protective clothing, blue for food and water, red for medical supplies, and black for miscellaneous equipment.
hZWZyW2dCeqeo1Zlcm9x: For a straight-in non-precision approach, the MDH cannot be below the OCH (Obstacle Clearance Height). The OCH is the minimum determined by obstacle clearance requirements.
I0af6DSzRxAS7uLaZYis: ICAO Doc 8168 specifies a minimum obstacle clearance of 300 m (984 ft) in the primary area of the initial approach segment. This is higher than the intermediate (150 m) and final approach (non-precision: varies) segment clearances.
I8BV41mebHbCwbneCB37: To act as a flight instructor for PPL issue, you must hold a valid licence plus a flight instructor rating. A CPL alone without an instructor rating does not authorise flight instruction.
i8IsAgqldvyGhruiM0t6: Loading limitations must include all limiting masses, centres of gravity positions, mass distributions, and floor loadings. All four elements are necessary to verify the aircraft is loaded within its structural envelope.
I9HCtecFmQt0d7pS4xnG: ICAO Annex 1 allows medical examination deferment of a single period of six months for non-commercial flight crew in remote areas. For commercial crew, the deferment is limited to three months.
iAHSxYDGbdVWbnfwqfgo: On an RNP 1 route, the designation A342 Z indicates turns should be made within the allowable RNP tolerance using a tangential arc with a radius of 15 NM on routes with turns between 30 and 90 degrees at and below FL 190.
IB8Psxuaqbf5ZTDYfJEJ: ICAO Annex 11 requires the lower limit of a Control Area (CTA) to be not less than 200 metres above ground or water. This provides minimum separation between uncontrolled surface airspace and the CTA.
ibrNKBdf6f4HFFcSgg3I: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that centreline and crossbar lights of a CAT I precision approach lighting system are fixed lights showing variable white intensity.
IfJszpDsmdKAliiJt2ln: Under JAR-FCL, single-pilot single-engine class ratings are valid for two years. After age 40, some national regulations reduce this to one year, but the base JAR-FCL validity is two years.
iFpV40bo5MAHkQF46tdF: When an aircraft is well above the PAPI approach slope, all four light units appear white. As the aircraft descends to the correct slope, the two nearest units transition to red while the farthest two remain white.
igFLt1ZzkaDwSKe6nApv: The correct SSR special purpose codes are: 7700 for Distress/Emergency, 7500 for Hijacking/Unlawful Interference, and 7600 for Communication Failure. Never confuse the distress and hijack codes.
IgMFmvXvOayfRw10VyFO: Landing gear structural damage from sinking into a hole meets the ICAO Annex 13 definition of an accident — substantial damage to the aircraft structure. The crew must follow accident reporting procedures.
IgS0YAZPxP4EgUE8AICw: A clearance that expires at a given time means if the aircraft is not airborne by that time, the clearance is void and a new clearance must be obtained. The pilot does not need to return to the ramp.
IJzSZoSX7TXNXGEht5ri: During independent parallel approaches, vectoring should establish the aircraft on the localizer in level flight for at least 2.0 NM prior to glide path intercept. This stabilisation distance ensures reliable localizer tracking.
iM0dAuR9PFJ4aCoElrlB: A red flare directed at an aircraft in flight means 'notwithstanding any previous instructions, do not land for the time being.' This overrides any prior landing clearance.
iN9Ci29W5xaFwPLpuSGk: The First Freedom of the Air is the right to fly over another State's territory without landing. The Second Freedom is the right to land for technical purposes. The Third and Fourth Freedoms cover carrying passengers between States.
iOc9cbQG8x321CSeesLx: A double white cross displayed horizontally in the signal area indicates glider operations are being conducted. Powered aircraft should exercise caution for glider activity in the vicinity.
IOj8s6hTh98aa97f4neA: Changing from IFR to VFR requires the pilot-in-command to initiate it with a message containing the specific expression 'cancelling my IFR flight.' ATC cannot unilaterally change a flight from IFR to VFR.
IQujQtMrGuh6k4Xsy7h1: The primary duty of a radar unit is to provide radar separation between aircraft. Assisting with navigation, equipment failures, or weather avoidance are secondary functions.
IsBuHxpg6ZW6TOJal80T: ICAO Doc 4444: the final vector for localizer intercept shall enable the aircraft to intercept at an angle not greater than 30 degrees. This prevents overshooting the localizer beam.
itztmSVSOICM1fBTEiTt: A serviceable transponder shall be operated at all times during flight, regardless of whether the aircraft is in SSR-equipped airspace. This ensures the aircraft is always visible to any available radar.
IUaND9Fx6buHywTQByiR: The final approach segment is where alignment and descent for landing are made. It extends from the FAF/FAP to the MAP (missed approach point) or the runway.
iwyPT7FGcOsej4c3V9Ci: Between 3050 ft and 10,000 ft AMSL outside controlled airspace, ICAO VMC minima are 5 km visibility, 1500 m horizontal and 1000 ft vertical distance from clouds. The 'clear of clouds' provision applies only below 3000 ft in Class G.
ixROrgiHmSx3oqhCVfLc: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that low-intensity obstacle lights on vehicles (not emergency/security vehicles) should be flashing yellow. This makes them visible but distinguishable from fixed obstacle lights.
IY0Z9vsO1ISHgLhaGLYh: In the PAPI system, two red units nearest the runway and two white units farthest from the runway indicates the aircraft is on or close to the correct approach slope. All red means too low; all white means too high.
IzHf756ZfBCie5OPyGa5: Projectiles showing red and green lights/stars at 10-second intervals is a signal that the aircraft is flying in or about to enter a restricted, prohibited, or danger area. The aircraft should take remedial action.
j3dTnpO54NYEJfDx9PMv: ICAO Annex 1 requires a licence holder to inform the authority after one calendar month of consecutive illness that prevents flying. Some question banks cite 21 days based on national regulations.
J47jv5JS6gsi2d0MMI9e: The main factor dictating the design of instrument departure procedures is the terrain surrounding the aerodrome. Obstacle clearance gradients and turning points are designed around terrain constraints.
J6GUd9TXCqu8exXYmQYr: ICAO Annex 1 requires CPL applicants to be at least 18 years of age. This is higher than the PPL minimum (17 years) and ensures maturity for commercial operations.
J7a49Ztlmd66u5TrTSzP: ATC clearances are issued to achieve separation between controlled flights. This is the primary purpose. FIS, alerting, and advisory services are provided through other mechanisms.
j9RvZwxksXaohuUFiYwL: For single-pilot commercial passenger transport, the Class 1 medical validity changes from 12 months to 6 months at age 40. This more frequent medical surveillance addresses increased risk.
J9UqKuXtw4YtFzdVlc0f: ICAO Doc 4444 prohibits speed adjustment requests after the aircraft has passed 4 NM from the threshold on final approach. This protects the stabilised approach.
jAv1JukNAGzF4b9xB6ek: A visual approach may be performed during an IFR flight when the pilot has permanent sight of the movement area and underlying ground. The pilot must maintain visual reference throughout.
JaWGHTJyX8GVU6pqI9If: Location indicators are listed in the GEN part of the AIP. GEN contains reference tables and general information applicable across the entire publication.
jbh3yIeVNW9Fs0Pzk5k8: If an aircraft enters the traffic circuit without authorisation, it shall be permitted to land if its actions indicate it desires to do so. Safety takes priority over procedural compliance.
jCgOJ4gPgHkTHrLpXvOR: For a four-engine aeroplane with the closest alternate three hours away, take-off minima must account for an engine-out approach at the departure aerodrome: ceiling at or above DH/MDH and visibility at or above landing minima for an available instrument approach with one engine inoperative.
JcP9TP7DnMULfSAKhiOn: ICAO Annex 15 requires each State to provide an Integrated Aeronautical Information Package comprising the AIP, AIP Amendments, AIP Supplements, NOTAMs, Pre-flight Information Bulletins, and AICs.
jGyjCnA3Ig0bCKUkgOEh: Alerting Service is provided by the ATS unit responsible for the aircraft at that moment, which may be any ATS unit (ACC, approach, aerodrome). It is not limited to units with 121.5 MHz equipment.
jLLd2EochtPju9bvOH7X: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies 2 minutes wake turbulence separation when a lighter aircraft is taking off in the opposite direction on the same runway or a parallel runway while a heavier aircraft is making a low or missed approach.
jm3ZsqOTQvC3y86zlWWh: In Class C airspace below 10,000 ft AMSL, a 250 kt IAS speed limitation applies to both IFR and VFR flights. Some question banks mark this as 'not applicable' based on national variations, but the ICAO standard imposes the 250 kt limit.
JqqIqHuH2voOAVC40aVq: In Class B airspace at or above 3050 m (10,000 ft), VMC minima are 8 km visibility with 1500 m horizontal and 1000 ft (300 m) vertical distance from clouds. Below 10,000 ft in Class B, the requirement may be 'clear of clouds' depending on the regulatory framework.
jSl1QRZ2KDCITZeZAYg5: The ICAO marshalling signal for 'set/apply brakes' is to raise arm and hand horizontally in front of body with fingers extended, then clench fist. This visually communicates the braking action.
jsMI1dUFdCjJSESPd7JQ: Information concerning charges for aerodromes and air navigation services is published in the AD (Aerodrome) part of the AIP, within each aerodrome's entry.
jSwHVUR79g7ZFMVY018W: The pilot-in-command is responsible for ensuring terrain clearance when following an ATC clearance. ATC provides separation from other traffic, but terrain clearance remains the PIC's responsibility.
jtAvnuHvWc8mRxp7e6ZD: Information about prohibited, restricted, and dangerous areas is published in the ENR (En-route) section of the AIP. These areas affect en-route navigation and are listed with their boundaries and activity details.
jTaYr4jtvgmQgPkd1U39: Under JAR-FCL, a CPL(A) applicant completing an integrated course must have at least 150 hours of flight time as pilot of aeroplanes with a JAA-accepted certificate of airworthiness.
jUl6XpO6Xx5wRC0SvYEL: ICAO Doc 4444: longitudinal time-based separation at the same level with 20 kt speed differential (leader faster) and frequent position determination = 5 minutes. Without differential = 10 minutes.
JUMJmRrs3iQXUIOEgICw: ICAO Annex 7 specifies that marks under the wings of heavier-than-air aircraft shall have a minimum height of 50 cm.
jvVJjbsmWNrdy6SK18sk: In Class B below 3050 m (10,000 ft) AMSL, VFR minima vary by regulatory framework. Some require 5 km visibility with 1500 m horizontal and 300 m vertical from clouds; others allow 'clear of clouds' in Class B.
JWhIo2cd5D8hMkTLAdYr: ICAO Annex 15 states that identification numbers for prohibited, restricted, and danger areas shall not be re-used for at least 3 months after cancellation. This prevents confusion with recently cancelled areas.
jY7PQSOgdRFH1SWGAcSu: ICAO wake turbulence distance-based separation for landing: Heavy preceding Light = 6 NM. This is the minimum radar separation to allow the vortices from the Heavy aircraft to dissipate.
k3d7fLhWtzBZPiaawsSG: ICAO Annex 14 states that aerodrome lights may be turned off provided they can be brought back into operation at least 15 minutes before the expected arrival of an aircraft. Some sources cite one hour.
K3RAsGvyLUIrW7CiZ1Nr: To execute public transport flights with an ATPL, the minimum age is 21 years and the pilot must not have attained 60 (for single-pilot ops). Some jurisdictions allow multi-crew ops until 65.
k5mMPsLeZZAhjSKjUMOy: If visual contact is lost during circling, the pilot should make an initial climbing turn towards the landing runway to regain a safe altitude, then initiate the published missed approach procedure.
K5NwHO2WAwBPP5Dkj2oH: A control zone (CTR) is a controlled airspace extending upwards from the surface of the earth to a specified upper limit. A control area (CTA) extends from a specified lower limit, not from the surface.
k6K2JSDCFlnjzDv9hybV: A controlled airspace extending upwards from a specified limit above the earth is a Control Area (CTA). An advisory airspace provides advisory service, not ATC. A control zone extends from the surface.
k6k3w2uL8fCbpLfo7jWJ: ICAO Annex 14: for two parallel runways, L (left) and R (right) are added as viewed from the approach direction. For three parallels, L, C (centre), and R are used.
K6kvOHl2GUXgRnI0kGzH: When a visual approach is cleared, the key condition is that ATC continues to provide separation from other controlled traffic. The pilot maintains visual reference, but ATC separation responsibility continues.
K8W0YZV4SEEyaH1noLt1: Night currency requirements specify take-offs and landings must be in the same category, class, and type of aircraft (if a type rating is required) to ensure the pilot has recent experience in that specific aircraft.
kCnAVfGAokw2rqoF3oRV: ICAO Doc 4444 allows 80 NM RNAV distance-based separation when aircraft are crossing levels and each reports distance from the same on-track waypoint.
kdKZWX5HvxdoBvbK1yg1: ICAO Doc 8168 specifies protection areas assume turns at 25 degrees bank or the bank angle for 3 degrees/second rate, whichever is lower, for departure and approach. Circling with prescribed tracks uses 25 degrees, and missed approach uses 15 degrees.
KdwpXmRCm6ncbbCLdxpl: ICAO Annex 1: for night privileges on a CPL, the applicant must complete at least 5 hours night flight time including 5 take-offs and 5 landings as PIC.
kDwsjrKO7PyNAQCzjyxT: A second-in-command transitioning to pilot-in-command on the same type must complete an upgrade training program. Initial training is for new types, and recurrent training is for maintaining existing qualifications.
kEIyS5hGqV4i5woJCPoR: Under JAR-FCL, an unrestricted FI(A) may conduct CPL instruction provided they have at least 500 hours total flight time including at least 200 hours of flight instruction.
kFe758SQYLu14yKF1FMa: Article 38 of the Chicago Convention requires States to inform ICAO of differences from the standards in any Annex. This is the notification of differences obligation, not about licences or ticket pricing.
KFnwEIAoudTnDGFsVtV3: The ground-air visual signal code for 'Affirmative' (YES) is the letter Y. X means 'Require assistance', N means 'Negative' (NO), and V means 'Require assistance'.
kHGemE0sQOE7nD8xgMe0: Separation minima near an airport may be reduced when the commander of the following aircraft has the preceding aircraft in sight and can maintain own separation. Controller discretion alone is insufficient.
KiUyvRTKhrLGzSHvPyic: Minimum Sector Altitudes are established within 25 NM of the IAF/navigation facility. This radius provides adequate obstacle clearance for aircraft in the terminal area before beginning an approach procedure.
KpOsfGqfqAXTnrRiIhZ7: ICAO Doc 4444 allows 10 NM DME longitudinal separation when the leading aircraft maintains 20 kt or more TAS faster than the following aircraft. A 10 kt differential is insufficient for the 10 NM minimum.
kPQTKg11MOCWVQzYt7YK: The international distress frequencies are 121.5 MHz (VHF) and 243.0 MHz (UHF). 2182 kHz is a maritime distress frequency. 2430 kHz is not a standard distress frequency.
KpRFPtihOJmB5Gbz3GTx: ICAO Annex 2: an intercepted aircraft shall attempt contact on 121.5 MHz, and if unsuccessful, repeat on 243 MHz. These are the international emergency frequencies for VHF and UHF respectively.
KqRjohBBRaR3VQHx29TG: When subjected to unlawful interference (hijacking), the transponder should be set to code 7500. Code 7700 is for general emergency, and 7600 is for communication failure.
KR6w3aQqn4Y60bG06qW1: A Special Air Report section I contains the position report including aircraft identification, height, position, and time. Section II contains the weather observations.
Kr8i42W0JwD8Na9tkpoA: A series of red flashes from the control tower to an aircraft in the circuit means the airport is not available for landing. This is a stronger signal than a steady red light (continue circling).
KRiDGNrDl4xFn1aHCted: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that centreline and crossbar lights of a CAT I precision approach lighting system are fixed lights showing variable white intensity, not green or flashing.
kuaRutwyOAUkZqXko0QQ: ICAO Annex 11 states that procedures in a UIR need not be identical with those in the underlying FIR. Different traffic characteristics at higher altitudes may warrant different procedures.
kWGpeOJSpdaeako6yFPM: ICAO Annex 17 requires both prior notification by the state of embarkation to the foreign state AND notification of the pilot-in-command for weapons carriage. Agreement between states alone is insufficient.
kwrPxIxU70y7p4sjOtbr: The Alert phase (ALERFA) is declared when apprehension exists as to the safety of an aircraft and its occupants. This is less severe than the Distress phase (DETRESFA) but more than the Uncertainty phase (INCERFA).
kXx35bAdWoQipfwihs0V: ICAO Annex 1 requires a CPL applicant to hold a current Class 1 medical assessment. Class 2 is for PPL holders only. The Class 1 standard ensures fitness for commercial operations.
kywWI5LfhreMVaWl4kJA: ICAO Doc 4444: during a radar approach, the pilot should consider executing a missed approach if position/identification is in doubt or if the aircraft is not visible on radar for a significant interval during the last 2 NM.
l3mlNMmowCMznbGJRZyj: ICAO Annex 14: parallel runways are designated with letters — L and R for two parallels, L, C, and R for three parallels. Numbers or no-letter conventions are not used.
L8T7ZQZo1rmnGiQLBNG6: DME (Distance Measuring Equipment) operates in the UHF band using decimetric wavelengths (around 1 GHz frequency range). This is the L-band portion of the radio spectrum.
L9Ty7wwDenkSSpe8igw4: Approach control should transmit an Expected Approach Time when holding of 10 minutes or more is anticipated. During visual approaches the pilot is not maintaining own separation in all classes — ATC still provides separation in Class C.
lal3mSpo6b4MpbcZ3Ac0: When a State renders valid a licence issued by another State, the validity shall not extend beyond the period of validity of the original licence. The rendering State cannot extend validity at its own discretion.
lBtn5eomznzvYuFPt7Tm: Above FL 290 in non-RVSM airspace, the Vertical Separation Minimum is 2000 ft. In RVSM airspace (FL 290-FL 410), it is reduced to 1000 ft. 4000 ft is not a standard VSM.
lCWERyHpVgIZ4M8U3X0h: On the correct glide path defined by PAPI, a pilot sees 2 red lights (nearest the runway) and 2 white lights (farthest from runway). All red means too low; all white means too high.
LEqZg4lBu47K1oAFFd25: A right-hand arrow of conspicuous colour displayed in the signal area indicates that turns in the aerodrome circuit are to be made to the right, both before landing and after take-off.
lfLONLB6qsETTSXkgkYg: The standard outbound timing in a holding pattern at or below FL 140 is 1 minute. Above FL 140 it increases to 1.5 minutes (or 2 minutes in some national procedures).
Lfm7hkVW2m9OUgOHvcGl: In non-RVSM airspace above FL 290, an aircraft subjected to unlawful interference that cannot communicate with ATS should fly at a level differing from normal IFR cruising levels by 500 ft below FL 290 or 1000 ft above FL 290.
lgcnGzKOJcOoq6ESNdrs: ICAO Doc 4444: aircraft under radar control shall not be vectored closer than 2.5 NM to the boundary of controlled airspace unless otherwise prescribed or agreed.
lI1NkSD3hFqkQ5hlaDpT: When receiving an IFR clearance, pilots should read back the initial route clearance, level assignments, and transponder codes. This ensures critical elements are correctly understood.
lLbdpEqnH54yLaewBXCm: ICAO Doc 4444 requires the EAT to be transmitted as soon as practicable when expected approach delay is 10 minutes or more.
LNJsz0BQSymlJCzCfuBh: ICAO Annex 1: a CPL(A) applicant needs 200 hours flight time or 150 hours if completed during an approved integrated course. The integrated course credit reduces the total requirement.
lnpPQSfeT7nuXmxzo4jT: A year-long runway closure is published in both NOTAM (for immediate notification) and AIP Supplement (for the permanent record). AIP alone misses the NOTAM notification component.
loCSPRQM526dAzGuzCmY: ICAO Doc 8168 specifies a maximum descent gradient of 5% in the final approach segment for non-precision approaches. This prevents excessively steep descents that would compromise stabilised approach criteria.
lOERf5eb19oGAbG6h6c8: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies SRA termination distances that vary by ATS authority. Common values are 2 NM or 4 NM from touchdown depending on the radar capability and local procedures.
lpFv3bew9Rbi3SwdgXcd: ICAO Annex 2: VFR flights in a CTR require ATC clearance when ceiling is below 1500 ft or ground visibility below 5 km. Special VFR may be obtained under these conditions.
LQSjuX6fYjvRFdZdgDTE: An aircraft in the traffic pattern indicating difficulties that compel landing without requiring immediate assistance does so by repeatedly switching landing lights on and off.
LrVblqi8kHf0KFkhk3qa: ICAO Annex 1: medical exam deferment for non-commercial crew is a single period of six months. Two consecutive periods or periods longer than six months are not permitted.
LscytmO2QeLvfEtuvR3J: JAR-FCL instructor categories: FI(A), TRI(A), CRI(A), IRI(A) ratings, plus SFI and MCCI authorisations. Examiners (FE, TRE, CRE, IRE) are separate categories.
lV2UZxkvi5IhzEStNYiO: An aircraft in the traffic pattern with radio failure signalling difficulties (not emergency) repeatedly switches landing lights on and off. This alerts the tower to the communication failure.
LWaKlD2t75HfJUUDAdyc: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies a minimum radar separation of 3.0 NM between aircraft on the same localizer course. For adjacent parallel localizer courses, different minima apply.
LwGAiZPFaDuig2mCI47i: Cabotage refers to domestic air services — commercial air transport between two points within the same country. Under the Chicago Convention, cabotage rights are reserved to national carriers.
lww8C9DMeEOrh5SqOmMK: A Special Air Report is required when severe icing or severe turbulence is encountered. These conditions pose significant hazards to other aircraft and require immediate notification.
lXNS5wj3ZR0fXck8qYgf: A braking action coefficient of 0.25 and below is classified as Poor. This indicates significantly reduced braking effectiveness and requires operational caution.
lY8W3lpC3Yr8pYfGY4Tg: Aerodrome Reference Code number 4 corresponds to a reference field length of 1800 m and over. Code 3 is 1200-1800 m, Code 2 is 800-1200 m, and Code 1 is below 800 m.
lZBodn2vNDpvq9I6aVx8: ICAO Doc 4444 requires ATS clocks to be accurate to within plus or minus 30 seconds of UTC at all times. This level of accuracy ensures consistent time-based separation.
m1It1q5IEt0DDtgkrtpi: Under ICAO Annex 9, contracting states may not accept oral declarations of baggage. Written declarations or other documentation is required for customs and security purposes.
m3Y5Z37WcByXlfuq86x3: Prohibited, restricted, and danger areas are published in the ENR (En-route) section of the AIP. This information is essential for route planning and airspace avoidance.
M9c5hwpNcKTf3MYNuGD6: In the PAPI system, 2 red nearest + 2 white farthest = on or close to the correct approach slope. All red = below slope, all white = above slope, 3 red + 1 white = slightly below.
m9SH9dKqb4FTARtiQAsq: A stopway is a defined rectangular area at the end of the take-off run available, prepared for an aircraft to stop in case of an abandoned take-off. It is included in ASDA but not in TODA.
MA2E7jfVC2tTibRuuB6b: A control zone (CTR) extends upwards from the surface to a specified upper limit. A control area (CTA) extends from a specified lower limit above the earth, not from the surface.
McJJUWvi7dWk7iNbRXBI: The Aerodrome Reference Code uses numbers 1-4 and letters A-F. Code 2B is valid (number 2 for field length 800-1200 m, letter B for wingspan 15-24 m). 5E and 6D are invalid as numbers exceed 4.
Mfm6WMegx1oohjhVXGcv: The current ICAO AIP structure consists of three parts: GEN (General), ENR (En-route), and AD (Aerodromes). The older structure with separate AGA, COM, MET, FAL, MAP, RAC, and SAR sections has been superseded.
mfT4d5PKNieIM0DY9rz4: ICAO Annex 14: runway lead-in lighting consists of groups of at least three white lights flashing in sequence towards the runway, guiding pilots from the approach path to the threshold.
mJ3ftNp1oshJhA7AjasY: ICAO Annex 14: low-intensity obstacle lights on mobile objects should be flashing red or preferably yellow. Yellow makes them more visible and distinguishable from fixed obstacle lights.
mLM0wUooyJGV2uei8F8u: The initial approach segment commences at the Initial Approach Fix (IAF), not the FAF. The FAF marks the beginning of the final approach segment. The sequence is IAF → IF → FAF/FAP → MAP.
mmJzrjuvk91JcUZMI3jB: JAR-FCL establishes separate type ratings based on three criteria, one being that the aircraft has handling characteristics requiring additional training. Certification by manufacturer or non-member state is not a criterion.
mRiuJRwxxaEO9dkTuhRE: Standard vertical separation applies. The aircraft at FL 150 can expect clearance to descend to FL 140 when the lower aircraft reports leaving FL 140, providing the required 1000 ft vertical separation.
MRskgstC0OX2qin8fkOL: IAC charts include OCA/OCH values, DME frequencies, and obstacles in the final approach sector. However, visibility minima for alternate aerodrome use are typically published separately in the AIP text.
ms51iyhDmPmjY2AVgKI7: JAR-FCL class ratings cover single-pilot aeroplanes not requiring type ratings. This includes self-sustaining gliders and other types as determined necessary by the authority.
MTfU5HiGsMKD0dC8MaL8: ICAO Doc 4444: a specific flight level is considered occupied when the aircraft is within plus or minus 300 ft of that level. This criterion may be reduced by appropriate ATS authorities.
mw4y7gorh1qdb7vhzMyo: ICAO Doc 4444: for dependent parallel approaches, missed approach tracks must diverge by at least 30 degrees. This ensures adequate separation during the missed approach phase.
mwWzjGZYJ1ETSU3KWpiT: The Rome Convention (1952) covers damage caused by foreign aircraft to third parties on the surface. The Tokyo Convention deals with offences on board aircraft. Do not confuse the two.
my6mCPr709HPuL8hl0Zt: ICAO Annex 2: IFR flights over non-mountainous terrain shall maintain at least 1000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km. Over mountainous terrain the minimum is 2000 ft within 8 km.
mycJW3q9KfdDvYBucIdT: If an emergency exit is in the flight crew compartment, the door between cockpit and cabin must be latched open during takeoff and landing to ensure passengers can access the exit.
Mzxr7k2IRiNKyof2nfuN: For powered aircraft on VFR night flights, an electric landing light is required if the flight is for hire. This ensures the pilot can see the landing area during night operations.
N3MSs5Ln6FDk3j6YMP7v: Taxiway centreline lights (except exit taxiway lights) are fixed green. This distinguishes them from taxiway edge lights (blue) and helps pilots track the centreline.
N40RdM9YOnmSinvjSSse: In Class B above 10,000 ft AMSL, VMC minima are 8 km visibility with 1500 m horizontal and 1000 ft vertical distance from clouds. The 'clear of clouds' provision for Class B applies only below 10,000 ft.
N6ijCRgV1lYmlPEvwZjy: A series of red flashes from the tower to an aircraft in the circuit means the airport is not available for landing. The aircraft should not land and should proceed as instructed or to an alternate.
N7cQtY1E8Zh1N4ryDyLl: Runway lead-in lighting consists of groups of at least three white lights flashing in sequence towards the runway. This guides pilots from the approach area to the threshold.
N9e0SVaeO410C9rCHPL3: ICAO Doc 4444: for independent parallel approaches, a No Transgression Zone (NTZ) of at least 610 m wide is established equidistant between the extended runway centrelines.
nBMkSBVD24aALhIDHwSV: ICAO Annex 11: the lower limit of a CTA shall not be less than 700 ft AGL (approximately 200 m). This provides minimum separation between surface operations and the CTA.
nDwotTzBQyQ9JvbEukvm: A base turn is a turn between the outbound track and the intermediate/final approach track where the tracks are NOT reciprocal. A procedure turn has reciprocal tracks.
nFuEYj43tjO1P3pTUsyk: Below 10,000 ft, non-safety related cockpit activities are prohibited. This sterile cockpit rule ensures flight crew focus on critical phases of flight including takeoff, landing, and low-altitude operations.
nGq9d0KgwpH5iUuUT06M: ICAO Annex 2: when common language is not possible during interception, the intercepted aircraft should use 'CAN NOT' to indicate inability to comply. This is a standard interception phrase.
Nl3lKLwZ6pHE9URDpUp9: Above FL 290 in non-RVSM airspace, VSM is 2000 ft. In RVSM airspace (FL 290-FL 410), it reduces to 1000 ft. The 2000 ft standard applies where RVSM is not implemented.
nn1uTcxQjZ8zJ5WrhS8R: ICAO Annex 17: a State shall take adequate measures for the safety of passengers and crew of an aircraft subjected to unlawful interference until their journey can be continued.
NN8dmPlzhixTfZRIkvBp: ICAO Annex 7: registration marks shall not use four-letter combinations beginning with Q, as Q-codes are reserved for international telecommunications signals. Five-letter combinations from the international code of signals are also avoided.
Nndn9IhRqu1dTMuXiJJ5: In Class E below 10,000 ft AMSL, IFR flights are subject to the standard 250 kt IAS speed limitation. This reduces closing speeds in terminal airspace.
NndPtlKlq9AzjFBPdLnS: The standard outbound timing in a holding pattern at 14,000 ft or below is 1 minute in still air conditions. Above 14,000 ft it increases to 1.5 minutes.
Noz4d8wImatQDHlDWncc: ATIS broadcasts should be updated immediately when a significant change occurs — such as a runway change, significant weather change, or change in approach type. Regular updates without changes are also required.
nQZMyXoFAc5RJVivg2r3: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies a tolerance of plus or minus 300 ft for Mode C level verification. This means the displayed altitude must be within 300 ft of the assigned level to be considered accurate.
Nrk0mg9hJox21yDhNpm5: ICAO Doc 4444: the radar separation minimum may be reduced by the appropriate ATS authority but shall not be reduced below 3.0 NM. This is the absolute minimum radar separation.
NrKOd4KFOEpsYsGlZbfX: ICAO Annex 9: documents for entry and departure of aircraft are accepted at the contracting State's discretion regarding format. They may be handwritten or produced electronically.
NsMLjcOi4QhOelQKU1SO: ICAO Annex 15: each State shall provide an Integrated Aeronautical Information Package comprising AIP, AIP Amendments, AIP Supplements, NOTAMs, PIBs, and AICs.
nSrMcJbrAjagBS1uqKuD: Per ICAO Annex 2 Appendix 1: the interceptor's signal for 'You may proceed' is an abrupt breakaway consisting of a climbing turn of 90 degrees or more without crossing the intercepted aircraft's flight path.
nTdofo2B96q1RcH7YERU: A technical landing (refuelling, maintenance, crew change without commercial traffic) is the Second Freedom of the Air. The First Freedom is overfly without landing, Third is disembarking passengers from home state.
nTQR89AOqHgIwTb8jF6R: In Class E, the 250 kt IAS speed limit applies to both IFR and VFR flights below FL 100 (10,000 ft). Above FL 100, no specific Class E speed limit applies.
NYcOHEY3AxT3MxYb7cEv: ICAO Doc 8168: the obstacle clearance in the primary area of the intermediate approach segment is 150 m (492 ft). This is less than the initial segment (300 m) and more than the final approach segment.
O2MAfnI9pZw6VClnA2mf: ICAO Annex 1: CPL applicants need at least 20 hours cross-country as PIC including a flight of at least 540 km (300 NM) with full-stop landings at two different aerodromes.

zWu43MZKpba7Oo8hBr7l: The pilot-in-command has final authority as to the disposition of the aeroplane. This is a fundamental principle of air law.
zxBTGw8LeXDdi7NPpfGb: Above 14,000 ft, the outbound time on a 30-degree offset track in a holding entry is limited to 1 minute 30 seconds.
04Swvku0Iu8YELBscSAS: Friction in the boundary layer backs the surface wind relative to the gradient wind in the northern hemisphere and slows it. Over the sea, where friction is light, the rule of thumb is back about 10 degrees and reduce speed to roughly 70-80%: 350 backed 10 degrees gives 340, and 24 kt reduced gives about 20 kt, so 340/20. Over land the effect is roughly double: back 30 degrees and halve the speed.
05FLTZYsycg746fGkldM: The subtropical jet (around 30 degrees latitude, near FL390) and the polar front jet (around 40-60 degrees, near FL300) are permanent features present all year, though both are stronger and displaced equatorward in winter. The arctic jet is essentially a winter feature, and the equatorial easterly jet only appears in the northern-hemisphere summer over southern Asia and Africa in connection with the monsoon.
07z536E3Be7h7KBk6iNL: Geostrophic wind is the theoretical wind that results when the pressure gradient force is exactly balanced by the Coriolis force. That balance is only possible with straight, parallel isobars and no friction, so the wind blows parallel to the isobars at constant speed. Curved isobars introduce centripetal acceleration and give the gradient wind instead; friction gives the surface wind.
0bDVZuEX3xFfIudTqoO6: In mid-latitudes the tropopause sits near 11 km (about 36,000 ft), and the stratosphere extends from there up to the stratopause at roughly 50 km. Above that lies the mesosphere (50-85 km) and then the thermosphere. Note the tropopause height varies with latitude: about 8 km over the poles and 16-18 km over the equator.
0EGLH1bSrarzMn7wIWIu: A squall line is a non-frontal line of active thunderstorms and is one of the phenomena for which a SIGMET is mandatory, along with severe turbulence, severe icing, severe mountain wave, volcanic ash, and tropical cyclone. A SIGMET is a warning of en-route weather hazardous to aircraft; a TAF is a routine aerodrome forecast and is not the vehicle for hazard warnings.
0fQzO7ODIM4s97odv3Lv: The environmental lapse rate (ELR) is the actual measured temperature profile of the real atmosphere at a given place and time, so it varies continuously with time, location and height, and can even be negative through an inversion. The fixed figures quoted in the distractors belong elsewhere: 0.65 C/100 m is the ISA lapse rate and 1 C/100 m is the dry adiabatic lapse rate.
0G0IwG5PW3BQdEPMSMhc: RVR is normally greater than the reported meteorological visibility because it is assessed against high-intensity runway lights, which remain visible through obscuration long after unlit dark objects have disappeared. RVR is reported in METAR/SPECI only (never TAF), is triggered when visibility or RVR falls below 1500 m, and is measured by transmissometers or forward-scatter meters; a ceilometer measures cloud base, not visibility.
0jPIfeFcJkuYFXwBLVOU: Work the two errors in turn. Pressure: with QNH 1003 but 1013 set, the datum is 10 hPa (about 270 ft) below sea level, so the altimeter over-reads by 270 ft. Temperature: 15 C colder than ISA means the aircraft is lower than indicated, so indicated = true / (1 - 4 x 15 / 1000) = 15000 / 0.94 = about 15,960 ft. Adding the 270 ft pressure error gives roughly 16,230 ft. Remember: cold air and low pressure both make the altimeter read high.
0KdNKNzLkK3BJFugU9mg: On the ground the altimeter reads the height of the aircraft above whatever datum is set on the subscale. Setting 1013 when the actual QNH is 993 is 20 hPa too high, and at about 27 ft per hPa that adds 540 ft to the reading. The airfield elevation is 540 ft, so the altimeter shows 540 + 540 = 1080 ft. With 1013 set on the ground the reading is by definition the pressure altitude of the airfield.
0oGOCZfGwvoNFuZUKPjX: By WMO convention low cloud has its base between the surface and 6500 ft, medium cloud between 6500 ft and about 23,000 ft, and high cloud above that. The classification is by base height, not by top, and the medium and high boundaries vary with latitude (they are lower over the poles and higher over the tropics).
0oLyE7DpZSkeglaIRGXN: A trough is an elongated extension of low pressure. Air spirals inward toward low pressure, so along the trough line the flow converges, and because that converging air cannot go into the ground it must rise. The lifting is why troughs are associated with cloud, precipitation and thunderstorms. A ridge is the opposite: divergence with subsidence and generally fine weather.
0ptnvvkynoJ9JytT6FaU: A flight level is measured from the 1013.2 hPa datum, so it only sits at or above its nominal altitude when neither pressure nor temperature pushes it down. QNH at or above 1013 puts the datum at or below sea level, and temperature at or above ISA expands the air so each level is physically higher. Both conditions together guarantee the flight level is at least at the stated height. A 'warm high' is not a safe substitute, because a high-pressure area is high only relative to its surroundings and can still have a QNH below 1013.
0Qj30BGAvhh1Krrp1I22: RVR groups in a METAR always represent the touchdown zone, which is the most operationally critical part of the runway for landing. Where mid-point and stop-end sensors exist they are used for low-visibility operations and passed by ATC, but they do not appear in the routine METAR group. The METAR gives a one-minute or ten-minute representative value, with a tendency indicator (U, D or N) when it has been changing.
0vbYDdjmuBh9kfR7SWqe: The lowest usable flight level must be safe under the worst combination of conditions, and both low pressure and low temperature push a flight level physically downward. So you need the lowest QNH expected along the route and the largest negative (coldest) deviation from ISA. Correcting for the best-case conditions instead would leave the aircraft below the minimum safe altitude.
0VqrpAffE8ScrWohsclC: The standard constant-pressure charts and their approximate ISA heights are 850 hPa near 5000 ft (FL50), 700 hPa near 10,000 ft (FL100), 500 hPa near 18,000 ft (FL180), 300 hPa near 30,000 ft (FL300) and 200 hPa near 39,000 ft (FL390). A pressure level of 4781 ft therefore corresponds to the 850 hPa chart.
0XNqbVx6qDu1cV275ubd: Freezing fog (FZFG) consists of supercooled water droplets: liquid water existing below 0 C. It is reported when those droplets freeze on contact with a surface, which is why it is a serious airframe and runway icing hazard. If the droplets had already frozen the fog would be ice fog, which is a different phenomenon and is far less hazardous for icing.
15Gt5NNgFbroYMRmtNKl: Take the pressure error first: FL160 is 16,000 ft above the 1013 datum, and with QNH 1003 that datum sits 270 ft below sea level, so the altitude above sea level in ISA terms is 15,730 ft. Now the temperature: ISA at 16,000 ft is about -17 C, so -27 C is a deviation of -10 C. True altitude = 15,730 x (1 - 4 x 10 / 1000) = about 15,090 ft. The aircraft is lower than the flight level suggests, which is the classic cold-weather hazard.
194R2U0KinzQgmhm3UIP: Descending air is compressed and warms at the dry adiabatic rate. Its actual moisture content is unchanged, but warmer air can hold far more water vapour, so the saturation capacity rises while the amount present stays the same, and relative humidity falls. This is why subsidence in a high-pressure area dissolves cloud, and it is also the mechanism behind the dry, warm Foehn wind.
1nyrjezxGnOWBKohi0mr: A deep winter trough near Iceland draws cold polar maritime air southward over a relatively warm ocean. That combination is steep-lapse-rate and unstable, giving convective cloud, snow and hail showers, and the tight pressure gradient around the trough gives strong, gusty surface winds and marked low-level wind shear. Light winds and a high ceiling belong to a stagnant high, not a trough.
1uWxgefwPccZJV6tu6Ix: A jet stream exists because of a strong horizontal temperature gradient, but that gradient reverses sign across the tropopause: below the core the cold air is on the polar side, above the core it is on the equatorial side. At the level of the core itself the two effects cancel, so the horizontal temperature gradient is close to zero. Flying through a jet with little temperature change therefore tells you that you are at core level.
1WPj582oCfXkeAc29XFz: GR is the METAR code for hail (diameter 5 mm or more), and hail requires the strong, deep updraughts that only cumulonimbus can produce, so it is reported almost exclusively with CB (or towering cumulus in the case of small hail, GS). Stratus, cirrocumulus and altostratus have nowhere near the vertical motion needed to keep a hailstone aloft while it grows.
1XoHazcqbn6xX1rNJ091: A stationary anticyclone is maintained by convergence aloft feeding subsidence through the depth of the troposphere. The sinking air is compressed and warms, its relative humidity falls, and cloud evaporates. That subsidence is the direct cause of the cloud-free upper levels. Divergence aloft would produce the opposite, forcing ascent, and is a feature of a developing low rather than a high.
288u5vf4jsR43bCcRWBD: Subsidence warms air adiabatically and lowers its relative humidity, which evaporates cloud droplets. It also builds a subsidence inversion that caps any further vertical development. Convection and cooling both do the opposite by driving air toward saturation, and a pressure decrease implies ascent and cooling, which encourages cloud rather than dispersing it.
2cTRXXFFY7hULXUQxYyc: The trade winds are the low-level flow from the subtropical high-pressure belts toward the equatorial trough, blowing from the north-east in the northern hemisphere and the south-east in the southern hemisphere. Where they meet is the ITCZ. The doldrums are the calm belt at the ITCZ itself, not a wind system, and the westerlies lie on the poleward side of the subtropical highs.
2el5uXx7TocfuyIMT4DC: A tropical revolving storm needs a sea surface temperature of at least about 26.5 C through a deep layer. Both the south-east Pacific and the South Atlantic are dominated by cold ocean currents (the Humboldt and Benguela) and associated upwelling, so the water never gets warm enough to supply the latent heat. Coriolis force is present at those latitudes, so its absence is not the reason.
2F3f0RTEwyD0kSyf3gvO: Surface friction slows the air, and because the Coriolis force is proportional to wind speed, it weakens too. The pressure gradient force is unaffected, so the balance is broken and the resultant wind is deflected toward low pressure, crossing the isobars at roughly 10 degrees over the sea and 30 degrees over land. Above the friction layer that imbalance disappears and the wind blows parallel to the isobars.
2fuPX99dtEDjAFz1vXG5: The polar front is the boundary between cold polar maritime or polar continental air and warm tropical maritime air, and it is the zone along which mid-latitude depressions form. The corresponding boundary further north, between arctic and polar air, is the arctic front, which is a distinct and generally weaker feature.
2l6k9qD3yQgx7zLbkJMj: ISA temperature at a flight level is 15 minus 1.98 C per 1000 ft, so at FL300 it is 15 - 59.4 = about -45 C (the tropopause and its constant -56.5 C are not reached until FL360). An air mass 15 C warmer than ISA therefore gives -45 + 15 = -30 C. Above FL360 the ISA temperature stays constant, so this arithmetic only works below the ISA tropopause.
2QCVVugjWqsEWzf872Gd: Frontal or precipitation fog forms ahead of a warm front, where warm rain falls through the cold air below the frontal surface, evaporates into it and raises its dewpoint until it saturates. It can occur at any time of day or night because it does not depend on radiational cooling, which is what distinguishes it from radiation fog.
2qHagTAYCsaDV1Aq8AFG: The atmosphere is largely transparent to incoming short-wave solar radiation, so the sun heats the earth's surface rather than the air. The surface then warms the troposphere from below, by conduction into the lowest layer, by convection, and by long-wave terrestrial radiation absorbed by water vapour and carbon dioxide. This bottom-up heating is why temperature normally decreases with height.
2r4zBxJE5TxqVbzRopVq: A squall line is a line of vigorous thunderstorms typically 50-300 NM ahead of and roughly parallel to a fast-moving active cold front. It forms where the cold air's downdraught outflow undercuts the warm sector well in advance of the surface front. Squall lines are frequently more severe than the front itself and are a mandatory SIGMET item.
2xiIg8tm1ohogCQIr3S5: With QNH 1013 the pressure datum is effectively at sea level, so there is no pressure error, and FL120 reads 12,000 ft. The true altitude is also 12,000 ft, so there is no temperature error either. That can only be the case if the mean temperature of the layer between sea level and the aircraft equals the ISA mean. It says nothing about the temperature at any individual level, only the average.
2yh1CDGdoPOBegxUr46Z: Cloud amount is reported in oktas (eighths of the sky): FEW is 1-2 oktas, SCT is 3-4, BKN (broken) is 5-7, and OVC (overcast) is 8. SKC or NSC indicates no cloud of significance. The distinction matters operationally because a ceiling is defined as the lowest BKN or OVC layer.
39hQLDRBMCXtNKkmPPGb: The dewpoint is the temperature to which a parcel of air must be cooled, at constant pressure and constant moisture content, for it to become saturated. A small temperature-dewpoint spread means air close to saturation and a fog or low-cloud risk; a spread of 3 C or less with a clear night and light wind is a classic radiation fog signature.
39ook1kVDVGFcj4n5o3f: The dry adiabatic lapse rate is fixed at 3 C per 1000 ft (1 C per 100 m) because it is set by the thermodynamics of a parcel expanding without heat exchange, not by conditions in the surrounding air. The saturated adiabatic lapse rate is variable (roughly 1.2 to 2.8 C per 1000 ft) because latent heat release depends on how much water vapour there is, and the environmental lapse rate is variable because it is simply whatever the real atmosphere is doing.
3BqOVtYtt2ONud6KeT3M: A thunderstorm cell has three stages. In the cumulus stage there are updraughts only. In the mature stage, marked by the onset of precipitation at the surface, updraughts and downdraughts coexist side by side, producing the most severe turbulence, wind shear, hail, lightning and gust fronts. In the dissipating stage downdraughts dominate and the cell decays, leaving an anvil.
3cvsFtmiWSdNnuk06dpP: A tropical revolving storm is driven by latent heat released as water vapour, evaporated from a warm ocean, condenses in the deep convective cloud of the eyewall. That heat release warms the core, deepens the surface low and strengthens the inflow, a self-sustaining loop. This is exactly why the storm decays rapidly on making landfall or moving over cool water: the moisture supply is cut off.
3g9Jv5Hd9FHNvpmQn2Av: The 300 hPa level sits near 30,000 ft, where ISA temperature is about -44 C. A reading of -30 C is therefore some 14 C warmer than standard, which for that level is a high temperature. Interpreting an upper-air temperature always requires comparing it to the ISA value for the level, not judging the raw number.
3NIWvUAIZd8SAPenfFG7: The group 241322 is a validity period, not an observation time: valid on the 24th from 1300 to 2200 UTC, which is 9 hours. The presence of BECMG and TEMPO change groups with their own time windows also identifies it as a forecast. A METAR or SPECI would carry a single day-and-time observation group ending in Z and no change groups of this type.
3OGZXR26HdGr62ZryJFS: Satellite imagery gives continuous coverage over oceans, deserts and polar regions where surface and upper-air observing stations are sparse or absent, so its main operational value is identifying and tracking frontal cloud bands and depressions in data-void areas. Precipitation location is better done by ground radar, which detects the droplets themselves rather than cloud tops.
3WKZf0MhZJFMVcXdCG3W: Aquaplaning requires a continuous film of water on the runway, which needs heavy rain: +RA. Dynamic aquaplaning is generally possible above a speed of about 9 times the square root of the tyre pressure in psi. SA is sand, BCFG is fog patches and FG is fog, all of which reduce visibility but none of which produce standing water.
3X8pNNKCdbToujtHdAYE: The Mistral is a cold, strong, dry northerly wind that blows down the Rhone valley to the Gulf of Lions, driven by a pressure gradient between high pressure over France and low pressure over the Gulf of Genoa, and accelerated by the valley's funnelling. The Bora is a comparable cold fall wind but blows from the north-east over the Adriatic; the Foehn is warm and the typhoon is a tropical cyclone.
4jZK6HZpXroGDwUcP2a3: Convergence at low level forces air upward because it cannot go into the surface. Rising air expands, cools adiabatically and, once it reaches its dewpoint, condenses into cloud. This is why convergence lines, troughs and the ITCZ are all cloudy features. Divergence at low level implies subsidence and tends to dissolve cloud instead.
4LYQFi91W0IMmPZFnw5o: Conditional instability means the environmental lapse rate lies between the saturated and dry adiabatic rates. A dry parcel cools at 3 C/1000 ft, faster than the environment, so it becomes colder and denser and sinks back: stable. A saturated parcel cools more slowly because of latent heat release, so it stays warmer than the environment and keeps rising: unstable. The instability is thus conditional on the air being saturated.
4qv2SZpG9zB5dXLipEmL: Above the friction layer only the pressure gradient force and the Coriolis force act, and they come into balance with the Coriolis force equal and opposite to the pressure gradient force. That balance can only exist when the wind blows along the contours, with low heights to the left in the northern hemisphere. Contour lines (isohypses) join points of equal height on a constant-pressure chart and are the upper-air equivalent of isobars.
5CuxCYaz5PlYtLrx4t3l: Closely spaced isobars mean a steep pressure gradient and therefore a strong wind. At the surface, friction still deflects the flow toward low pressure, so the wind crosses the isobars at about 10 degrees over the sea and 30 degrees over land. Only above the friction layer does the wind blow parallel to the isobars.
5eotRTjzvJdVBuQuyA5o: The 200 hPa surface lies at roughly 39,000 ft (FL390) in temperate latitudes, which is why the 200 hPa chart is the standard upper-wind chart for long-haul cruise levels and for locating jet cores. Its height varies with the mean temperature of the layer beneath: higher over warm air, lower over cold air.
5GbRUXcvtrQUu2PfuiIp: As a parcel rises, the surrounding pressure falls, so the parcel expands. That expansion does work against the surrounding air and, with no heat exchanged with the environment, the work is done at the expense of the parcel's internal energy, so its temperature falls. This adiabatic cooling is 3 C per 1000 ft while unsaturated. The temperature of the surrounding air determines stability, not the cooling itself.
5KAPsupn0SdimMJGICCW: Steaming fog, also called arctic sea smoke, forms when a very cold air mass moves over much warmer water. Rapid evaporation saturates the shallow layer immediately above the surface and it condenses as it mixes upward. It therefore requires cold air mass properties and a strongly unstable, not stable, low-level lapse rate, which is why the fog appears to steam upward.
5Kf84974r0e6uCjxnecv: The Chinook is the Foehn wind of the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains: air forced over the range loses its moisture as precipitation on the windward side, then descends the lee side warming at the dry adiabatic rate, arriving warm and very dry. The Bora is a cold fall wind, the Harmattan is a dry dusty north-easterly off the Sahara, and the Scirocco is a warm southerly off North Africa.
5n15QRTOcF7ZpKBALG6X: Saturation is reached by cooling the air to its dewpoint (or by adding moisture). Adiabatic expansion is exactly that: the parcel rises, expands against falling ambient pressure, does work and cools, so its relative humidity rises to 100%. Raising the temperature or compressing the air adiabatically warms it and lowers relative humidity, and reducing pressure at constant temperature does not lower the temperature, so none of those can saturate it.
5r9Yahnvd3OKQKrp6zTq: Tropopause height follows the mean temperature of the troposphere beneath it: about 8 km over the poles, about 11 km (36,000 ft) in mid-latitudes such as 50 N, and about 16-18 km over the equator. The tropopause temperature runs the other way, roughly -45 C over the poles, -56.5 C in mid-latitudes and -75 C or colder over the equator.
5vPGH8PzuuQK9WYvsenV: ICAO grades icing in three intensities. Light icing is no problem unless encountered for more than an hour, so no change of heading or level is needed. Moderate icing makes even short encounters potentially hazardous and a diversion is desirable. Severe icing requires immediate diversion because de-icing and anti-icing equipment can no longer cope.
65KUF9GMeECAKlYjz4ty: Forecast upper winds, on significant weather charts, wind/temperature charts and in flight documentation, are always given relative to TRUE north and in knots. Only ATC-passed surface winds (for take-off and landing) are given relative to magnetic north, because they are being compared directly with a runway direction.
68PNJoOD37e0V4cvYcWI: The eyewall, the ring of towering cumulonimbus immediately surrounding the eye, contains the strongest surface winds, the most violent updraughts and downdraughts, the heaviest precipitation and the lowest pressure gradient scale in the storm. The eye itself is comparatively calm with light winds and often broken cloud, and conditions moderate steadily with distance from the centre.
6hwRZWmmKHAVBwGrRG2U: The most severe airframe icing occurs where supercooled water droplets are most abundant, in the band from 0 C to about -10 C or -15 C. Interpolating the sounding, 0 C lies near 10,600 ft and FL150 is around -8 C, squarely in that band. FL80 is above freezing so no icing occurs, and FL180 (-14 C) and FL220 (about -22 C) are increasingly glaciated, giving lighter rime rather than severe clear ice.
6yeTsZdbxe1tfxUZpkiL: Clear ice forms when large supercooled droplets freeze slowly on impact, so the water flows back over the surface before it freezes and builds a dense, transparent, tenacious layer. It is heavy, adds significant weight and drag, distorts the aerofoil section, spreads well aft of the protected leading edges, and is hard for de-icing boots to shed. Rime ice, by contrast, is opaque, brittle and light because it traps air.
76Ic4pcwBjVotS85dyYg: A temperature-dewpoint spread of less than 1 C means the air is effectively saturated, so condensation is occurring or about to occur at the surface. That produces fog or very low cloud. Pilots use the spread as a quick indicator: 3 C or less with clear skies, light wind and a long night is the classic radiation fog set-up.
7AE1UmCFVRz3XB5nvYVu: Cumuliform cloud forms in unstable air where vigorous updraughts carry droplets upward, allowing them to grow large by collision and coalescence. Large droplets freeze slowly on impact and produce clear ice; the vertical motion gives turbulence; and precipitation falls as showers of limited horizontal extent. Stratiform cloud in stable air has the opposite set: small droplets, little turbulence, continuous widespread rain and rime ice.
7dZYMgEqQgE1cZyjZ880: Radiation fog needs a light wind: enough gentle turbulence to mix the cooling upward through a shallow layer, but not enough to stir it out. Below about 5 kt is the classic requirement. In dead calm the cooling stays right at the surface and produces dew or frost instead of fog, and above roughly 10 kt the mixing lifts the layer into low stratus.
7h4egbuB1lw6WY1l3xDy: Freezing rain needs a warm layer aloft above a sub-zero layer below, so rain falls as liquid, becomes supercooled while descending through the cold air, and freezes on impact. That structure exists ahead of a warm front in winter, where warm air is overrunning cold air trapped at the surface. It is among the most dangerous icing conditions because the droplets are very large and the ice accretes far aft of protected surfaces.
7Jb5H8CkYQNH2BHo20IG: An increase in surface wind strengthens mechanical turbulence, which mixes the saturated surface layer upward through a deeper column. If it lifts the fog clear of the ground it becomes low stratus; if the mixing is strong enough it dissipates the fog entirely. Surface cooling, increasing stability and a low-level inversion all reinforce fog rather than clear it.
7K0cWlWoWEkP8MGe3OxE: A lapse rate of 1 C per 100 m is exactly the dry adiabatic lapse rate (3 C per 1000 ft). An unsaturated parcel displaced vertically in that environment cools or warms at exactly the same rate as its surroundings, so it always has the same temperature and density as the ambient air and neither returns nor continues: neutral stability for dry air. For saturated air the same layer would be unstable, because a saturated parcel cools more slowly.
7KtryPmPtsuJNlAmlBA0: Radiation fog is shallow because it is produced by cooling from the ground upward through a light-wind, stable, inversion-capped layer. Typical depths are 100-1000 ft, averaging about 500 ft. That is why the sky is often visible vertically through it while horizontal visibility at the surface is close to zero, and why it lifts into low stratus so readily as the wind picks up.
7RdQYyIvPIqwELW14eDp: In mid-summer the Azores high is at its strongest and extends north-east toward Europe, while the Icelandic low is at its weakest and displaced, leaving a shallow low over north-east Canada and Baffin Bay. The pattern reverses in winter, when the Icelandic low deepens sharply and the Azores high retreats south, steepening the gradient and driving the strong westerlies of the North Atlantic track.
7W8aDanj80EuKxb9Mrj8: The intensity scales hinge on one word. Moderate turbulence: definite strain against seat belts, unsecured objects dislodged, food service and walking DIFFICULT. Severe turbulence: abrupt large changes in altitude and attitude, occupants forced violently against belts, food service and walking IMPOSSIBLE, and the aircraft may be momentarily out of control. Light turbulence gives only slight, erratic changes.
83kumOMhExGXwUErVUel: A sounding that crosses 0 C twice reveals a warm layer aloft over a sub-freezing layer beneath, the classic freezing-rain structure of a warm front in winter. Precipitation melts in the warm layer, becomes supercooled in the cold layer below and freezes instantly on the airframe. The resulting large-droplet clear ice runs back well beyond the protected leading edges and is graded severe.
8bH8dIllvEgJ73lF5DG9: RVR appears only in METAR and SPECI, as an RDD/VVVV group following the visibility. It is an instrumented, aerodrome-specific, near-real-time measurement, so it has no place in a TAF (a forecast) or a SIGMET (an en-route hazard warning). RVR is included whenever the visibility or the RVR itself is below 1500 m.
8cwHmUh92ulyJnb4CkpC: The ITCZ is where the two trade wind systems converge, forcing deep ascent in warm, very moist air, so frequent and widespread thunderstorms with tops often above FL500 are its defining feature. It migrates seasonally, following the sun with a lag, and it is not associated with a jet stream (the equatorial easterly jet is a separate, seasonal feature).
8I93zQo6PMxf6GQZJyM9: With QNH 1013.2 there is no pressure error, so the whole 1000 ft discrepancy is thermal. Using true altitude = pressure altitude x (1 + 4 x deviation / 1000): 12,000 = 13,000 x (1 + 4d/1000), giving 4d/1000 = -0.077 and d = about -20 C. The aircraft being lower than its indicated level is the signature of colder-than-standard air.
8KCKF4PPvWOugEM5n2Fu: The tropopause is simply the boundary surface between the troposphere, where temperature falls with height, and the stratosphere, where it is first isothermal and then rises. It is not itself an inversion or an isothermal layer by definition - it is the level at which the lapse rate changes - and the strong lapse rate belongs to the troposphere below it.
8RAjPAIzm8JkR0LhnLtG: Approaching a warm front, the gently sloping frontal surface (about 1:150) means cloud is met in a predictable descending sequence: cirrus and cirrostratus roughly 800 km ahead, then altostratus, then nimbostratus with continuous precipitation from about 300 km out to the surface front. Cumulonimbus and squall lines belong to the cold front, which has a much steeper slope of about 1:50.
8tibwYM5YvzsDWFhtNWw: On the ground the altimeter shows the height of the aircraft above the datum set on the subscale. Setting 1013 when the actual QNH is 1008 is 5 hPa too high, and at about 27 ft per hPa that adds roughly 135 ft. Airfield elevation 1240 ft plus 135 ft gives 1375 ft, which is the pressure altitude of the airfield.
8zA8eyenkfkcymS25FPL: Decode the abbreviations: MOD TO SEV CAT is moderate to severe clear air turbulence, FCST means forecast rather than observed, BTN FL260 AND FL380 gives the vertical extent of the hazard, STNR means the area is stationary, and INTSF means the intensity is increasing. The validity 030700/031100 runs from 0700 to 1100 UTC on the 3rd. Note that STNR rules out any answer describing the zone as moving.
91Cx6FXD6Y4VkTDbGFKh: A thermal low is maintained by surface heating, which drives convergence into the low at the surface. That converging air must rise, and the ascent can only continue if it is removed aloft by upper-level divergence. Widespread ascent cools the air adiabatically to saturation, producing extensive cloud and precipitation. The reverse pattern - surface divergence with upper convergence - describes an anticyclone.
9AlnPRa0IbsTizQQupED: The saturated adiabatic lapse rate is lower than the dry rate only because condensation releases latent heat, and the amount of latent heat available depends on how much water vapour the air holds. Cirrus forms at very low temperatures where the air can hold almost no moisture, so almost no latent heat is released and the SALR approaches the DALR of 3 C/1000 ft. In warm cumulus near the surface the SALR can be as low as 1.2 C/1000 ft.
9DvDBbEWKnceo7RC1vS8: The tropical tropopause is both the highest (16-18 km) and the coldest, at around -75 C to -80 C, because deep convection lifts air a long way and it cools all the way up. The mid-latitude tropopause is near -56.5 C at 11 km and the polar tropopause is the warmest, near -45 C at 8 km. Height and temperature therefore vary inversely with latitude.
9EjN4OsUeMVfTuBE6KDs: The ITCZ follows the overhead sun with a lag, so it crosses the equator twice a year, near the equinoxes. Equatorial Africa therefore has two rainy seasons, around March-May and October-November, separated by two relatively drier periods. Away from the equator the two passes merge into a single wet season.
9fTjXeKkwUD4sWjgPggD: 3000 ft is above the friction layer, so the wind there is the gradient wind, blowing parallel to the contours (isohypses). At the surface, friction reduces the speed, which weakens the Coriolis force and lets the pressure gradient force turn the flow across the isobars toward low pressure - backed by about 10 degrees over the sea and 30 degrees over land in the northern hemisphere, and weaker. Backed, not veered, is the key point.
9LKZGKIeryp87V9SolIM: Dewpoint can never exceed the air temperature, because as soon as air is cooled to its dewpoint it saturates and further cooling condenses out the excess. It can, however, equal the air temperature: that is precisely the saturated state, with relative humidity 100%, which is the condition inside cloud and fog.
9oUWxrsygIRzi6XIboru: Density altitude is pressure altitude corrected for the deviation from standard temperature. When the actual temperature equals the ISA temperature for that level, the correction is zero and the two are identical. Warmer than standard makes density altitude higher than pressure altitude, which degrades take-off and climb performance; this is true at any level, not only at sea level.
9P93oMkFtWpzrRytlJ1S: An inversion is a layer in which temperature increases with height, reversing the normal profile. Inversions are very stable, so they trap moisture, smoke and dust below them, giving haze and poor visibility, and they cap convection. Common types are radiation (nocturnal), subsidence (in an anticyclone), frontal and turbulence inversions.
9pNZe6NE4kIk4fY8MZm9: Haze (HZ) is a suspension of dry solid particles - dust, smoke, salt and industrial pollution - too small to be seen individually. It becomes a visibility problem when a stable layer, typically an inversion, prevents vertical mixing and lets the particles accumulate below it. Mist (BR) and fog (FG), by contrast, are made of water droplets and occur at high humidity.
9sbHDk70KDP1l45oyiHp: The wet south-west monsoon reaches southern India around the start of June and spreads north over the following weeks, drawing very moist maritime air off the Indian Ocean as the heated land generates a deep thermal low. It withdraws through September to November, giving way to the dry north-east monsoon in the winter half of the year.
9WZN8fa7fBuuZAy0Qn2J: The polar front jet is driven by the horizontal temperature contrast across the polar front. In winter the pole-to-equator temperature gradient is steepest, so the jet is strongest, and the whole frontal system is displaced toward the equator, so the jet moves south. Winter speeds commonly reach 150-200 kt against 60-100 kt in summer.
A2SWskADtywN03osBwa9: Subsidence is slow, widespread downward motion of air, characteristic of anticyclones and ridges. The descending air is compressed and warms adiabatically, so its relative humidity falls, cloud dissolves and a subsidence inversion forms, trapping haze beneath it. It is the opposite of convection, which is localised upward motion.
a9sYYxzaGNcff7YYc4nP: The centre of a stationary high has a very weak pressure gradient, so surface winds are light or calm, and subsidence builds a strong inversion at low level. That inversion traps moisture, dust and pollution beneath it, so summer conditions over land are typically hazy with poor horizontal visibility but no significant cloud. Thunderstorms need lifting, which the subsidence suppresses.
adEAVc1Bc8cMSntGRnaL: Radiation fog requires a clear sky (so the ground radiates heat away freely overnight), light wind of a few knots (to mix the cooling through a shallow layer), high humidity, and a long night. Cooling the surface layer to its dewpoint then condenses the moisture into fog.
